Annex I A: HTSUS modifications — images. But important: the note text (the chapter 99 note with rules like "rate net of MFN", "goods in transit", "section 232", "9802", etc.) might be in Annex I as text? The document's Annex I starts at 2190 with A... then graphics. Hmm, all images. But Q7(d) asks "Where is the rule for treating MFN rates that are not ad valorem stated, and where is the result for an equivalent rate at or above the cap stated?" — that would be in the Annex I note text (image?) or maybe in the Annex I text preceding graphics? Wait: maybe the annex includes textual note provisions after the graphics. Let me check the TOC entries beyond 2095 — TOC listed only up to "IV. Severability" and total 4520 lines. Annex I starts 2190 and continues to 4520? That's 2300 lines — mostly graphics? Possibly the annexed HTSUS provisions include readable text (e.g., note 5 to subchapter III). Let me grep for "net of" or "not ad valorem" or "specific" in 15181.

Also Q8(b) asks "Cite exactly where the rule for goods in transit is stated" — the DATES line at 91 FR 47318. And Q8(d): patented pharmaceutical article under heading 9903.04.62 — that's a chapter 99 heading for pharmaceuticals; maybe the annex note says goods under 9903.04.62 exempt? Need text.

Let me grep for "ad valorem" occurrences with context around specific-duty conversion, and for "9802", "9903.04", "privileged", "in transit", "Liechtenstein".

Sesame seeds for sowing (1207.40.00) exempt globally under (c)(4). Continue reading 2560-2900 to get Cambodia, Taiwan, others, and the net-of-MFN rules and (8) patented pharma.

tools.name: fr_search

query.description: Full-text search terms; "" for none. Supports quoted phrases, e.g. "\"extension of stay\" F-1".
query.title: Query

doc_type.description: Document types: RULE, PRORULE (proposed rule), NOTICE, PRESDOCU (presidential document). null for all.
doc_type.title: Doc Type

agency.description: Agency slugs, e.g. homeland-security-department, u-s-citizenship-and-immigration-services, u-s-immigration-and-customs-enforcement, state-department, labor-department, executive-office-of-the-president.
agency.title: Agency

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).
pres_type.title: Pres Type

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.
cfr.title: Cfr

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

answer.description: Direct answer to each lettered part, in order, labelled (a), (b), ...
answer.title: Answer

basis.description: Provisions and documents relied on, with citations.
basis.title: Basis

uncertainty.description: What the documents leave open, or "None".
uncertainty.title: Uncertainty

content.text:
Excellent. Now I have the essential note text: note 52 subdivisions. Key Q7(d): rule for non-ad valorem MFN rates at note 52(k), FR 47394 (line 2824-2845); the "result for equivalent rate at or above the cap" is stated as: "For headings 9903.05.39 and 9903.05.76, articles for which the applicable column 1 duty rate is less than 10 percent, the sum ... is 10 percent"; and for 9903.05.49, .71, .74 (Japan, Korea, Switzerland) less than 12.5% → sum is 12.5%. The "result at or above the cap" — the memorandum and notice say where MFN ≥ 10 percent (or 12.5), section 301 rate is zero. That's in the notice at FR 47320-47321.

Now which heading applies to which economy? Headings 9903.05.20-9903.05.84 correspond to economies; I need the mapping. The heading numbers are in the Annex I A table (images). Hmm. But from subdivision (k) references: 9903.05.38, 9903.05.39 (EU), 9903.05.48, 9903.05.49 (Japan?), 9903.05.70, 9903.05.71 (Korea?), 9903.05.73-76 (Switzerland/Taiwan). Also (j)(3): headings 9903.05.73-9903.05.74 = Switzerland; (j)(10): 9903.05.75-9903.05.76 = Taiwan. (j)(2): 9903.05.38-9903.05.39 = EU. (j)(1): 9903.05.81 = UK. (g): 9903.05.29 = Canada. (h): 9903.05.55 = Mexico. (i): 9903.05.33,34,37,40,42,58 = Costa Rica, DR, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua. (5): 9903.05.28 = Cambodia; (6): 9903.05.40 = Guatemala; (7): 9903.05.37 = El Salvador; (8): 9903.05.22 = Argentina; (9): 9903.05.26 = Bangladesh; (11): 9903.05.45 = Indonesia; (12): 9903.05.35 = Ecuador; (13): 9903.05.50 = Jordan; (4): 9903.05.54 = Malaysia.

For Q7(b): Italy (EU, 10% net, heading 9903.05.38/39); Japan (12.5% net, 9903.05.48/49); Brazil (12.5% flat).

Careful: For the EU, note (k) first paragraph applies to goods subject to specific or compound rate: AVE = duty payable / customs value. Then the cap: "For headings 9903.05.39 and 9903.05.76, articles for which the applicable column 1 duty rate is less than 10 percent, the sum ... is 10 percent." So for EU: heading 9903.05.38 presumably covers MFN ≥10% (zero duty) and 9903.05.39 covers MFN <10% (net). Similarly for Japan: 9903.05.48 (MFN ≥12.5 → zero), 9903.05.49 (net).

Now Q7(b) second: Italy: 4% + $0.25/kg on 4,000 kg = $1,000 specific + 4% of 20,000 = $800 → total $1,800 → AVE = 9% (<10%) → section 301 duty = 10% - 9% = 1% → $200. Japan: 12.5% - 9% = 3.5% → $700. Brazil: 12.5% flat → $2,500.

Q7(a): France: 3 cents/kg × 2,000 kg = $60 duty; customs value $12,000 → AVE = 0.5% → 301 = 9.5% → $11,400? Wait 10% - 0.5% = 9.5% → $11,400. Check: total duty 10% of 12,000 = $1,200; MFN $60; 301 = $1,140. Yes! 10% of 12,000 = 1,200, minus 60 = 1,140. Good (I mis-multiplied: 9.5% × 12,000 = $1,140).

Q7(c): Taiwan: MFN $2,200 on $20,000 = 11% ≥ 10% → 301 = 0. Switzerland: MFN 11% < 12.5% → 301 = 12.5% - 11% = 1.5% → $300. Careful: Switzerland heading 9903.05.73/74 — (k) refers to 9903.05.74 for the 12.5 cap. Yes.

Q6(b): Germany MFN 12% (EU ≥10%) → 301 = 0. Japan MFN 12% → 12.5-12 = 0.5% → $500. Taiwan MFN exactly 10% → "greater than or equal to 10 percent" → zero. South Korea MFN exactly 10% → 12.5-10 = 2.5% → $2,500. Switzerland MFN free → 12.5% → $12,500.

Q6(a) with MFN 4%:
1. Switzerland: 12.5 - 4 = 8.5% → $8,500; MFN $4,000; total $12,500.
2. Norway: is Norway in net list? No → 12.5% flat → $12,500; total $16,500. (Norway is among the 54 failing to impose.)
3. UK: 10% flat → $10,000; total $14,000. (UK 10%, not net.)
4. Germany (EU): 10 - 4 = 6% → $6,000; total $10,000.
5. Taiwan: 10 - 4 = 6% → $6,000; total $10,000.
6. Türkiye: 12.5% → $12,500; total $16,500.
7. Japan: 12.5 - 4 = 8.5% → $8,500; total $12,500.
8. Liechtenstein: not investigated → 0. Need to verify Liechtenstein isn't among the 60 economies.
9. Hong Kong: 12.5% → $12,500; total $16,500.
10. India: 10% → $10,000; total $14,000.

Now Q9: 
(a) 9802.00.80: additional duties apply to value of assembled article less cost/value of U.S. products = 100,000 - 35,000 = $65,000; Thailand rate 12.5% → $8,125.
(b) 9802.00.50 repairs: additional duties apply to value of repairs = $6,000; Israel 12.5% → $750.
(c) Mexico: (i) entered free of duty under USMCA → exemption under (g)/(h)? Note (h): "As provided in heading 9903.05.94, the additional duties imposed by heading 9903.05.55 shall not apply to any products of Mexico entered free of duty under the USMCA" → 0. (ii) no USMCA claim: 10% of 50,000 = $5,000. MFN 5% → 5% (Mexico is flat 10%, not net).
(d) Japanese passenger car under 232 heading 9903.94.01 → exempt per (f)(2) → 0.
(e) Brazil with 232 duty under a chapter 99 heading the note does not mention → not exempt by (f) (which lists specific headings) → 12.5% of $100,000 = $12,500. Also note (a) says products subject to the additional duties "shall also be subject to any additional duty provided for in this subchapter or in subchapter IV of chapter 99" — so stacking applies. So 12.5%.
(f) June proposal: exempted informational materials, donations, accompanied baggage, and all articles and parts subject to section 232 tariffs. Adopted text: (f) exempts only specific listed 232 headings (not all 232 articles); informational materials/donations? Need to check note 52 for "informational materials" and "donations". Let me grep.

Also Q9(f) asks what the adopted text says about informational materials and donations. Let me grep for those terms.

Q8(d): patented pharmaceutical article under heading 9903.04.62 entered July 30 vs Aug 3. Annex I part B (effective July 31, 2026) added patented pharmaceutical articles provided for in headings 9903.04.60-9903.04.66 to heading 9903.05.90 exemption. So July 30 → not exempt → 12.5% of $80,000 = $10,000. Aug 3 → exempt → $0. 

But careful: the exemption requires the article be "patented pharmaceutical articles provided for in headings 9903.04.60-9903.04.66" — 9903.04.62 falls within. Good.

Q8(a): Dominican Republic, MFN free, $80,000, 12.5% (DR is flat 12.5%), except textile/DR-CAFTA exemption under (i) — not relevant (not textile). In-transit rule: goods loaded on vessel at port of loading and in transit on final mode before 12:01 a.m. July 24 and entered before 12:01 a.m. July 28 → not subject.
1. Loaded July 22, entered July 29 → entered after July 28 → duty applies: 12.5% × 80,000 = $10,000.
2. Loaded July 22, entered July 27 3:00 p.m. → in transit before July 24, entered before July 28 → $0.
3. Entered 12:01 a.m. July 28 → "before 12:01 a.m. July 28" fails → duty applies $10,000.
4. Loaded 6:00 a.m. July 24 → after 12:01 a.m. July 24 → not in transit before; duty applies $10,000.
5. Entered July 23 (before July 24) → not applicable → $0 (duties apply only to entries on/after July 24).
6. Warehouse withdrawal July 26: goods entered warehouse earlier (arrived June). Withdrawal from warehouse for consumption on July 26 → subject (duty applies to withdrawn from warehouse for consumption on or after July 24). In-transit rule? Goods arrived in June and held in bonded warehouse — they were imported before, but the rule requires "loaded onto a vessel at the port of loading and in transit on the final mode of transit before July 24 AND entered ... before July 28". Hmm — withdrawal July 26 is before July 28, but is it "in transit on the final mode of transit before July 24"? No — it arrived in June, so not in transit. So duty applies: $10,000. Hmm, but could argue "entered for consumption" includes warehouse withdrawal; the transit exception requires both conditions. Not satisfied → $10,000.
7. Air freight: loaded on aircraft at 9 p.m. July 23, entered July 25 → exception requires "loaded onto a vessel" — aircraft is not a vessel → duty applies $10,000. Hmm, "vessel" — air cargo not covered. That's the trap. So $10,000.

(c) Signed July 23, 2026 (memorandum); effective 12:01 a.m. July 24, 2026; published July 28, 2026.

Now Q10(e): "a shipment that arrives on October 2, 2026" — whisky subject to import ban (ban applies to goods imported on/after Sept 29) → excluded from importation (no duty; cannot import). 

Q10(c): Sept 1, USMCA free: 338 duty applies (50% of 60,000 = $30,000) — is there a USMCA exemption from section 338? No. Section 301: Canada 10% but exempt for products of Canada entered free of duty under USMCA (note 52(g), heading 9903.05.93) → $0. Section 338: $30,000. Wait, but does the alcoholic beverages 338 duty apply to USMCA-qualifying goods? Nothing exempts them. So 338 = $30,000, 301 = $0, total $30,000.
(d) No USMCA claim: 338 = $30,000; 301 = 10% × 60,000 = $6,000; total $36,000.

Q10(a)/(b): aluminum extrusions listed in Annex II of MV proclamation (338), subject to 232 50% on full value, heading 9903.82.02. MFN 3%, value $200,000.
Sept 10: MFN 3% = $6,000. 232 = 50% × 200,000 = $100,000. Section 338: 11046/11048 clause (2) excludes articles subject to section 232 → $0 (before Sept 15 modification). Section 301: 232 exempt per note 52(f)(1) (heading 9903.82.02) → $0. Total $106,000.
Sept 16: 338 applies (Annex II MV items as modified; and 11065 says duties apply in addition to 232) → 50% × 200,000 = $100,000. 232 = $100,000. 301 = $0 (232 exemption). MFN $6,000. Total $206,000.

Wait — is the extrusion listed in Annex II of the MV proclamation? Scenario 1 says yes ("have been listed in Annex II of the motor-vehicles duty proclamation since it was signed, and are on no Part A, Part B or exclusion list"). Fine. And Sept 16 is after Sept 15 → 338 applies in addition to 232 per 11065 clause (1).

Q4: X (alcoholic Annex II, 232 25%, $100,000): Sept 10: 232 = $25,000; 338 = $0 (11046 clause (2)). Oct 1: 338 = 50% ($50,000) because 11064 clause (1) provides duties as modified apply in addition to 232; also is X on Part A or B of 11064? Scenario says "None of them is on any other list" → assume X not in Part A (continues subject) nor Part B (no longer subject). So 338 = $50,000; 232 = $25,000.
Y (dairy Annex II, 232): Sept 10: 232 $25,000; 338 $0. Oct 1: no dairy scope modification; 11047 clause (2) carve-out still stands → 338 $0; 232 $25,000.
Z (MV Annex II, 232): Sept 10: 232 $25,000; 338 $0. Oct 1: 338 $50,000 (11065 clause (1)); 232 $25,000.

Hmm — but careful: does 11064's change ("duties as modified in this proclamation shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to section 232") override clause (2) of 11046 for products that remain subject? Yes, later proclamation amends. The operative effect: 11046 clause (2)'s exclusion for 232 articles is superseded to the extent of inconsistency (clause (7) of 11064). So for X after Sept 15, both apply.

But for dairy Y, no such modification → carve-out remains. Good. That's likely the intended trap.

Now Q1: need for each document the "date and time from which its operative change applies" and "which kind of event that date and time is measured against":
- 11046: 12:01 a.m. ET Aug 19, 2026; measured against goods entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption (clauses 1, 3).
- 11056: 12:01 a.m. ET Aug 22, 2026; same event (entry/withdrawal) — the effective date of the duties. Note: recital calls it suspending for 3 days.
- 11061/11062/11063 (exclusions): 12:01 a.m. ET Sept 29, 2026; measured against goods "imported on or after" (not entry).
- 11064/11065 (scope modifications): 12:01 a.m. ET Sept 15, 2026; measured against entry/withdrawal.
- 11076 (Oct scope): 12:01 a.m. ET Oct 30, 2026; entry/withdrawal.

Which documents changed which products are subject to duty, per product group:
- Alcoholic beverages: 11046 imposed (Annex II); 11064 modified scope (Part A added to duty; Part B removed); 11061 excluded (import ban) — changes products from duty to ban. Also 11056 delayed all.
- Dairy: 11047 imposed; no scope modification (the referenced dairy scope proclamation doesn't exist); 11062 exclusion.
- Motor vehicles: 11048 imposed; 11065 modified (Part A added; Part B removed); 11076 further modified (Part A removed from duty; Part B added to duty); 11063 exclusion.

Q5: 
(a) 50% duty applicability at five times for P, Q, R, S:
- P: Annex I Part A of Sept MV scope → became subject Sept 15 12:01 a.m. So Sept 14 3:00 p.m. → not; Sept 15 12:01 a.m. → yes; Oct 29 4:00 p.m. → yes; Oct 30 12:01 a.m. → yes (unless listed in Oct Part A — scenario says P only listed in Sept Part A, "not listed in the original," and Q says nothing about Oct lists; R is in Oct Part A; S in Oct Part B). So P: no, yes, yes, yes, yes (Nov 3 yes).
- Q: Annex II original (subject from Aug 22) + Sept Part B (removed from duty effective Sept 15). So Sept 14 3:00 p.m. → yes (50%); Sept 15 12:01 a.m. → no; later → no.
- R: Annex II original + Oct Part A (removed effective Oct 30). So Sept 14 → yes; Sept 15 → yes; Oct 29 4:00 p.m. → yes; Oct 30 12:01 a.m. → no; Nov 3 → no.
- S: Oct Part B → added effective Oct 30 12:01 a.m. So Sept 14 → no; Sept 15 → no; Oct 29 → no; Oct 30 12:01 → yes; Nov 3 → yes.

(b) Oct scope proclamation: signed Oct 23, 2026; filed with OFR Oct 29, 2026 (11:15 am); published Oct 30, 2026 (91 FR 68861); applies from 12:01 a.m. ET Oct 30 to goods entered/withdrawn. Not retroactive: applies only to entries on/after; no refund provision (contrast 11056 clause (4)). Note 11064/11065 also no refund provision.

(c) Waiting period: Section 338 requires duties not to take effect earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation finding discrimination (quoted in each). P: signed Sept 8 → dutiable Sept 15 = 7 days after signing; S: signed Oct 23 → Oct 30 = 7 days. Do the scope proclamations explain? No — they recite the 30-day limit (recital 8 of 11065 / recital 9 of 11076) but do not explain how a 7-day effective date fits; implicitly they treat scope modifications of existing duties (already imposed after the July 20 finding) as amendments, not new duties — but the text doesn't say so explicitly. Also note 11046 was signed July 20 and duties Aug 22 = 33 days after signing; original Aug 19 = 30 days.

Q2: (a) Entries: 338 duty for wine listed in Annex II, 50%, $40,000 → $20,000 each if duty applies. Entry 1 Aug 20 2:00 p.m. → before Aug 22 → no duty ($0). Entry 2 Aug 21 11:59 p.m. → before Aug 22 12:01 a.m. → $0. Entry 3 Aug 22 12:01 a.m. → duty applies → $20,000.
(b) 11056 clause (1) amended only the chapeau of Annex II in each of the three proclamations, replacing "August 19, 2026" with "August 22, 2026"; the operative clauses (1) and (3) of 11046 (and counterparts) still read "August 19, 2026". Resolve: clause (1) of 11056 itself states the effective date "shall be 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 22, 2026" — a later presidential directive; and later documents (11061 recital 4, 11064 recital 4, 11065 recital 4, 11076 recital 4) state that at 12:01 a.m. Aug 22 the suspension lapsed and the duties became effective. Also the later proclamations are inconsistent-to-that-extent superseded (clause 5 of 11056 / clause 9 of 11046 supersession). So Aug 22 controls.
(c) Entry 1 deposit of 50%: The refund provision is 11056 clause (4): "To the extent that implementation of this proclamation requires a refund of duties collected, refunds shall be processed pursuant to applicable law and CBP's standard procedures for such refunds." And clause (2) directs agencies to suspend collection. Also 11061's text: the products imported but not entered remain subject to 50%; but for entry 1, deposited Aug 20 (before the effective date) → refund under 11056 clause (4). Note: does 11046's severability/no-refund? No. So: refund under 11056 clause (4) via CBP standard procedures. Also the documents don't provide interest or a specific mechanism; mention 19 CFR? Not in docs.
(d) Did duties need a further presidential action to begin? No: the duties began automatically when the 3-day suspension lapsed (11061 recital 4: "at 12:01 a.m. ... August 22, 2026, the 3-day suspension imposed by Proclamation 11056 lapsed, and the additional ad valorem duties ... became effective"). What do later documents say happened in days before they began: On Aug 21, 2026 Canada reneged on its commitment, ceased negotiating in good faith, and did not remove the discrimination (11061 recital 3; 11064 recital 3; 11065 recital 3; 11076 recital 3).
(e) Why Aug 19 originally: 30 days after July 20: recital 10/9 quotes section 338's requirement "not to take effect earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation"; July 20 + 30 days = Aug 19. Show arithmetic.

Q3: (a) A: arrives Sept 10, entered Sept 14 → before Sept 29 ban; 338 50% = $15,000; importable. B: arrives Sept 27 (before Sept 29), warehouse, withdrawn Oct 5 → imported before Sept 29 → not banned; clause (2) → remains subject to 50% = $15,000. C: arrives 11:30 p.m. Sept 28 → imported before Sept 29 → not banned; entry Sept 29 → clause (2): imported but not yet entered prior to Sept 29 → 50% duty $15,000. D: arrives 12:30 a.m. Sept 29 → imported on/after → excluded from importation; no entry permitted; duty $0 because no importation. 
(b) E: arrives Sept 25, FTZ Sept 25, entry for consumption from zone Oct 6: 11046 clause (4) requires privileged foreign status (admitted after Aug 22 effective date) → the goods were admitted Sept 25 so must be PF status; on entry for consumption Oct 6, duty = 50% = $15,000. Is it banned? The ban applies to goods "imported on or after Sept 29". FTZ admission isn't importation into customs territory; but nothing in the documents addresses FTZ + ban. Uncertainty flag: I'd say the 50% duty applies (clause 4 of 11046 and the fact that entry for consumption is the dutiable event) and the ban likely doesn't reach it because the goods were imported (arrived) before Sept 29 — but text is silent/ambiguous. Hmm, which is most defensible? The exclusion clause (1) uses "imported on or after", and clause (2) explicitly deals with goods "imported, but not yet entered for consumption ... prior to September 29" → remain subject to duty. That clause is exactly on point for goods in FTZ/warehouse imported before Sept 29: they remain subject to 50% duty, not the ban. So the 50% duty applies ($15,000) and no ban. Good, that's defensible.
Wait — for E, is a "privileged foreign status" requirement satisfied? Clause (4) requires admission as PF status for products admitted into FTZ on or after effective date; the scenario says admitted Sept 25; assumption: it was admitted properly. Then upon entry for consumption, 50% duty.

(c) Court invalidates import ban as applied to beer: 11061 clause (9)(b): the 50% duty under 11046 applies to the import to which the invalidated ban applied. So 50% duty applies to shipments imported after the ruling.
(d) Does the exclusion proclamation change the duty on listed Canadian alcoholic products not in its Annex? No: clause (3) says besides changing certain products from duty to ban, this proclamation does not otherwise affect the products established in the Sept 8 scope modification as subject to duties. So 50% continues.

Q13: Section 232 machine, steel article listed in Annex I-C of June 2026 proclamation (11032). Need to read 11032 to know the treatment: presumably a rate for articles in Annex I-C, USMCA-qualifying treatment, U.S.-content deduction, onshoring plans, and a sunset date. Let me read it.

Q15: Need IEEPA docs and 232 history, and Proclamation 11012 (surcharge), EO 14389. Let me now read 11032 and then the IEEPA items.

Budget: ~163k left. Let's move.

    93                  address the national security threats found in

    97                  valorem duty of 25 percent on derivative products that

   101                  industrial machinery and power equipment.

   112                  circumstances have affected and are affecting domestic 
   113                  industries that use agricultural equipment, industrial 
   114                  equipment and machinery, and other related products.

Q13 details: Annex I-C products (aluminum and steel articles listed): rate 25% under clause (2)(a), with:
- (2)(b): for products of certain countries incl. Japan, Korea, Switzerland, Taiwan, UK, EU, Argentina etc.: rate = so that column 1 + 232 = 15% (if C1 <15%), else 0. Note Canada is NOT in that list.
- (2)(d): For products of Canada and Mexico that qualify for USMCA preferential treatment, a duty of 25% applies only to non-U.S. content (total value minus value attributable to parts produced in the US); total effective duty shall not be less than 15% ad valorem.
- (2)(c): 10% for derivative articles whose aluminum/steel content composed entirely of US-smelted/cast metal, determined per Column 1 rates (weird).
- (4): 85% threshold for "entirely" US metal content.
- (3)(a): from Jan 1, 2028, rates set out in clause (3) of Proclamation 11021 apply.
- Clause (2) applies from June 8, 2026 until 11:59 p.m. Dec 31, 2027.

Now Q13 items (customs value $200,000, MFN free unless stated):
(a) Canada USMCA claim, U.S. parts $60,000: non-U.S. content = 200,000 - 60,000 = 140,000 → 25% = $35,000; but total effective duty not less than 15% of... 15% of what? "total effective duty on the imported product assessed under this subclause shall not be less than 15 percent ad valorem" — 15% of customs value = $30,000; $35,000 > $30,000 → duty $35,000.
(b) No U.S. content: non-U.S. content = 200,000 → 25% = $50,000; floor 15% = $30,000 → $50,000.
(c) Canada, no USMCA qualification: clause (2)(d) applies only to qualifying goods → rate 25% of full value (2)(a) = $50,000. (Canada not in (2)(b) list.)
(d) Japan, MFN 2.5%: (2)(b) → sum = 15% → 232 = 12.5% → $25,000.
(e) Canada USMCA, U.S. parts $20,000 + $30,000 attributable to aluminum smelted and cast in the US contained in a Canadian part. Hmm: non-U.S. content = total value minus value attributable to parts produced in the United States. The $30,000 is attributable to US-smelted aluminum contained in a Canadian-made part — is that a "part produced in the United States"? No; the part was made in Canada. So non-U.S. content = 200,000 - 20,000 = 180,000 → 25% = $45,000. The $30,000 of US aluminum doesn't reduce non-U.S. content under (2)(d) (which only counts parts produced in the US). But wait — does clause (4) (85% threshold) matter here? Clause (4) deems metal content composed entirely of US metal if US metal ≥85% of weight of metal. Here 30,000 out of? We don't know total metal weight value; scenario says "most of the steel and aluminum in it, by weight, was melted or smelted outside the United States". So the 85% test fails → clause (2)(c) 10% rate not available. So $45,000.
Hmm, but is the machine a "derivative article" for (2)(c)? It says derivative articles whose aluminum content composed entirely of US aluminum. Not satisfied.
(f) Same as (e), entered Oct 6, 2026: same rate (clause 2 effective from June 8, 2026) → $45,000. Why would the date matter? Perhaps because Oct 6 vs Oct 20 relates to something else — maybe a later proclamation changed rates? Hmm, Q13 says "Each unit is entered for consumption on October 20, 2026 unless another date is given," and (f) as in (e) but Oct 6. Is there any change between Oct 6 and Oct 20? Maybe Proclamation 11045 (July 20) modified aluminum duties. But both dates are after July 20. Hmm, maybe the point is that (f) is the same as (e) — no difference; testing that no change occurred. Or perhaps there is a change in section 338 duty? Q13 says "Give the section 232 duty only." So (f) = same $45,000. Possibly the trap is that Oct 6 is before Oct 20 and nothing changes.

Wait, maybe the answer for (f) relates to the 15% floor and... no. I'll just note same.

(g) U.S. parts $140,000: non-U.S. content = 60,000 → 25% = $15,000; floor: 15% of value = $30,000 → duty = $30,000 (floor applies). Note "total effective duty ... shall not be less than 15 percent ad valorem" and MFN is free, so the section 232 duty = $30,000.
(h) Until when does (a) treatment apply: clause (2) applies until 11:59 p.m. EST Dec 31, 2027; afterwards clause (3)(a) rates from Jan 1, 2028 per clause (3) of Proclamation 11021.

Hmm, but (h) says "Until when does the treatment in (a) apply, and what applies afterwards?" Yes.

Also need to check Proclamation 11021 (April) clause (3) rates to describe what applies after 2028? Could say "the rates set out in clause (3) of Proclamation 11021 (FR 18201)" without stating numbers (in image or text?). Let me check 11021 briefly later if budget allows.

Now Q15: need the full timeline of additional duties on Canadian aluminum extrusions:
- 232 aluminum duties: 25% (from March 12, 2025); then Proclamation 11021 (April 2, 2026, effective April 6?) set 50% on aluminum articles and derivatives; June proclamation 11032 changed things (extrusions in Annex I-A of April, not in Annex I-C of June → remain at ... hmm). The scenario says "throughout the period the extrusions are an aluminum article within the section 232 aluminum duties (in 2026, listed in Annex I-A of the April proclamation ... and not in Annex I-C of the June proclamation)". Annex I-C of June = the temporarily-reduced 25%/15% list. Annex I-A of April = 50% list. So 232 duty = 50% of value from April 6, 2026 through today.
- Section 338 duty: from Aug 22, 2026 (motor vehicles Annex II), 50% — but carve-out for 232 articles until Sept 15, then applies in addition (11065). So Sept 14 entry: 50%; Sept 16: 50%; Nov 10: 50%.
- Section 301 duty: Canada 10%, effective July 24, 2026, but exempt for goods of Canada entered free of duty under USMCA (note 52(g)); also exempt for 232 articles listed in (f)(1) (heading 9903.82.02 = derivative aluminum/steel articles) → 301 not owed at all for these extrusions (since entered under 9903.82.02). So 0 in all cases.
- IEEPA northern border duties: 25% (10% energy) from March 4, 2025; amended; ended by EO 14389 (Feb 20, 2026)? Need to check dates. Also possibly terminated earlier.
- 10% temporary import surcharge (Proclamation 11012, signed Feb 20, 2026): need effective date and whether Canada exempt, and duration (section 122 limit 150 days).
- MFN 3% (base, not asked but "in addition to MFN duty").
- Section 338 also possibly.

Entry dates: Feb 10, 2025; Mar 6, 2025; Mar 10, 2025; Mar 14, 2025; June 3, 2025; June 10, 2025; Aug 5, 2025; Mar 2, 2026; June 10, 2026; July 27, 2026; Aug 25, 2026; Sept 14, 2026; Sept 16, 2026; Nov 10, 2026.

I need: IEEPA duties timeline (14193: 25% from Feb 4, 2025? then delayed; 14197; 14231 amendment effective Mar 4, 2025 with USMCA exemption; 14325). Also whether IEEPA duties terminated (EO 14389 "Ending Certain Tariff Actions" Feb 20, 2026? Probably ends IEEPA tariffs following a court decision or trade deal). And the 10% surcharge (Proclamation 11012) effective when? Under section 122 (15% max, 150 days). Need details.

Also, does section 232 duty apply on Feb 10, 2025? Aluminum 232 was 25% on aluminum articles since 2018 (Proclamation 9704). The extrusions (7604) are aluminum articles subject to 232 25% throughout 2025, but Q15 assumes they are within the 232 aluminum duties throughout. In 2025 the rate was 25% (per Proclamation 9704 as amended, 25% from March 12, 2025; before that 10%). Hmm — Feb 10, 2025 rate was 10% (aluminum 232 was 10% until March 12, 2025 when it went to 25%). But the question says "Give every duty owed in addition to the MFN duty, by legal authority" — including 232. For Feb 10, 2025 entry, the 232 aluminum duty would be 10%. Do I know that from the FR? Real world: Proclamation 10895 (Feb 10, 2025) raised aluminum to 25% effective March 12, 2025. It's likely in this fictional FR too. I need to check.

content.text:
Proclamation 11012: 10% surcharge, for 150 days, effective February 24, 2026, with exemptions including (k) all articles subject to 232 → aluminum extrusions exempt from the surcharge. So for Q15, the surcharge (in force Feb 24, 2026 to ~July 24, 2026, 150 days) never applies to the extrusions because they're 232 articles. Also for Q10(f): asks whether Canadian goods entered September 2026 bear IEEPA northern border duties or the 10% surcharge: IEEPA duties no longer in effect (EO 14389, Feb 20, 2026); surcharge imposed for 150 days effective Feb 24, 2026 → expires 150 days later = July 24, 2026 (Feb 24 + 150 days = July 24). Also the extrusions/whisky are 232 articles? Whisky isn't; but surcharge ended July 24. Anyway. Also note: 11012's exemption list includes "Metals" section 232; whisky not 232-subject, but by September the surcharge has expired (150 days from Feb 24 = July 24, 2026).

Let me compute: Feb 24 + 150 days: Feb has 28 days in 2026 (not leap) → Feb 24 + 4 days = Feb 28 (4), March 31 (35), April 30 (65), May 31 (96), June 30 (126), July 24 (150). Yes, expires July 24, 2026.

Now I still need to check whether the IEEPA duties were ended with immediate effect (EO 14389 signed/published Feb 20/25, 2026; says duties "shall no longer be in effect"). For entry March 2, 2026, IEEPA no longer applies; the surcharge 10% applies (unless 232-exempt). Since extrusions are 232 articles → exempt from surcharge. So on March 2, 2026: only 232 (50%? or 25%?) — the April proclamation is effective April 6, 2026 (per Q15: "From April 6, 2026 the extrusions are entered under section 232 heading 9903.82.02"). Before that, what was the aluminum 232 rate? Need Proclamation 11021 (April 2, 2026) effective date and rates, and the pre-April rate.

Also for 2025 dates: aluminum extrusions 232 duty: 25% from March 12, 2025 (Proclamation 10895, Feb 10, 2025); before that 10%. Do I have those documents in this FR? Presumably yes: Proclamation 10895 of Feb 10, 2025 (90 FR 9415?) "Adjusting Imports of Aluminum Into the United States". Let me search quickly.

Actually, Q15 requires "every duty owed in addition to the MFN duty, by legal authority". The 232 duty is a duty imposed on these goods. So I need the 232 rates over time:
- Feb 10, 2025: 10% (aluminum 232, Proclamation 9704, as amended by 10895? Actually Proclamation 10895 raised to 25% effective March 12, 2025).
- Mar 6, 2025: 10%; Mar 10: 10%; Mar 14: 25%; June 3, 2025: 25%; June 10: 25%; Aug 5, 2025: 25% (plus 200% on... no that's aluminum derivative? In real world June 2025 raised to 50% for aluminum; but here maybe not). I must check the FR. Search for 2025 aluminum proclamations.

Let me search for "Adjusting Imports of Aluminum" 2025 presdocu.

So from April 6, 2026, aluminum articles in Annex I-A: 50%. Prior to that: 50% since June 4, 2025. So the 232 rate is 50% for all dates from June 4, 2025 onward, 25% Mar 12–June 3, 2025, 10% before Mar 12, 2025.

Wait — was there anything else changing 232 for extrusions (e.g., 11045 July 2026 aluminum)? Q15's assumption says "from April 6, 2026 the extrusions are entered under section 232 heading 9903.82.02" — fine; I should check 11045 briefly to see whether it changes rates on aluminum articles (it's "Further Strengthening Actions Taken To Adjust Imports of Aluminum"). Might add aluminum derivative coverage or a rate change. Since Q15 says no reduction granted to a particular producer/approved plan applies, and extrusions in Annex I-A — I'll check 11045 quickly with a grep for rates/effective.

Also for Q15 I need to check other additional duties on Canadian products in force at each date:
1. IEEPA Canada duties (Feb 4/Mar 4, 2025 → ended Feb 20, 2026).
2. Section 232 aluminum.
3. Section 301 forced labor (July 24, 2026), exempt for 232 articles (note 52(f)(1)) and for Canada USMCA.
4. Section 338 (Aug 22, 2026; carve-out until Sept 15 for 232 articles).
5. Temporary import surcharge (Feb 24–July 24, 2026), exempt for 232 articles.
6. Possibly the "reciprocal tariff" (EO 14257) — ended by EO 14389 too (as of Feb 20, 2026). Also possibly other Canada-specific actions in 2025 (e.g., 10% reciprocal tariff on Canada; USMCA exemption). Hmm — Q15 says "for each other additional duty then in force on products of Canada, say in a line why it is not owed." This includes reciprocal tariffs (IEEPA) which were in force 2025 (Canada 25%? or 10% baseline then 35%?). Ugh — need to know whether the reciprocal tariff applied to Canada in 2025 and terminated Feb 20, 2026. EO 14257 as amended: Canada's reciprocal rate... In the real world, Canada was not subject to the April 2025 reciprocal tariff (energy/Canada excluded?), actually Canada was excluded from reciprocal tariffs? Hmm. In the real world, EO 14257 Annex I lists Canada? Canada was not on the reciprocal list because of the fentanyl IEEPA duties. I'm not sure.

Given budget, I might handle Q15's "other duties" more generally: IEEPA northern-border duties (14193 as amended) and IEEPA reciprocal duties (14257) both terminated by EO 14389 (Feb 20, 2026) — for dates after that, not owed; for dates before, the reciprocal tariff... I need to know if Canada was covered. Let me do one targeted search/grep: EO 14257 mentions Canada? Actually search for documents imposing reciprocal tariffs on Canada. Might be that EO 14257 Annex I includes Canada with 0%? Hmm.

Alternatively, Q15 may be designed so that the "other additional duties" are: (i) IEEPA northern border duties, (ii) temporary import surcharge, (iii) section 301, (iv) section 338, and (v) reciprocal tariffs. I'll check EO 14257 for Canada quickly via grep.

Also, there might be an important detail: EO 14389's termination — but was there a court ruling requiring refunds? Not relevant.

Let me also check whether there are 2025 documents imposing a 10% reciprocal tariff and whether Canada exempt. Grep 14257 for "Canada".

content.text:
Good: EO 14257 §(d)-(e): reciprocal tariffs do not apply in addition to the northern/southern border IEEPA duties; if those orders are terminated, Canada non-USMCA goods subject to 12%, USMCA-origin zero. Since EO 14389 terminated IEEPA duties (including 14257 itself, so 12% never applies). Interesting but Q15: reciprocal tariff not owed (either it doesn't stack or it's terminated).

Wait: EO 14389 terminated 14257's IEEPA duties too. So from Feb 20, 2026, no reciprocal duties.

Hmm, but note EO 14257 (e) says if the border orders are terminated, Canada non-USMCA 12%. But 14257 itself was terminated by 14389 — and 14389 says all IEEPA duties under 14257 "shall no longer be in effect". So the 12% fallback never took effect? Possibly there was a later EO implementing the 12% fallback. Not important; the surcharge (11012) applied 10% from Feb 24 to July 24, 2026 instead.

Now for Q15, I have enough on the main layers. But I need to double check whether section 301's exemption for Canada USMCA-qualifying (note 52(g)) applies to extrusions — yes for Case U. And for Case N, extrusions are also exempt under note 52(f)(1) because 232 aluminum articles are exempt (heading 9903.82.02 is listed). So section 301 = $0 in both cases, all dates.

Now I also need to confirm the section 338 duty applies to extrusions: they're in Annex II of the MV proclamation; on Sept 14, 2026 the 338 duty applies in addition to 232 (because 11065's modification effective Sept 15 — wait, Sept 14 is BEFORE Sept 15!). So on Sept 14, 2026: 11048 clause (2) carve-out still in force → 338 = $0. On Sept 16: 338 = 50%. Good, that's the trap: Sept 14 vs Sept 16.

Now section 232 on extrusions: 50% throughout (from June 4, 2025). So:
1. Feb 10, 2025: 232 aluminum 10% = $10,000. IEEPA duties: EO 14193 as amended by 14197 → effective March 4, 2025; Feb 10 is before → not owed. Reciprocal: EO 14257 signed Apr 2, 2025 → not yet. Total additional = $10,000.
2. Mar 6, 2025: 232 10% = $10,000; IEEPA not yet (effective Mar 4? wait — EO 14197 paused to March 4, 2025 12:01 a.m.; so from Mar 4, IEEPA duties ARE in effect! Mar 6 → IEEPA 25% applies unless USMCA. Case N: 25% = $25,000; Case U: exempt (EO 14231 §2(a) entered free of duty under USMCA → exempt). So Case N total Mar 6: 232 $10,000 + IEEPA $25,000 = $35,000. Case U: $10,000.
3. Mar 10, 2025: same as Mar 6: Case N $35,000; Case U $10,000.
4. Mar 14, 2025: 232 25% ($25,000) + IEEPA 25% ($25,000) = $50,000 Case N; Case U: 232 $25,000.
5. June 3, 2025: 232 25% ($25,000) [50% effective June 4] + IEEPA 25% ($25,000) = $50,000 N; U: $25,000.
6. June 10, 2025: 232 50% ($50,000) + IEEPA 25% = $75,000 N; U: $50,000.
7. Aug 5, 2025: 232 50% + IEEPA 35% ($35,000) = $85,000 N; U: $50,000.
8. Mar 2, 2026: IEEPA terminated (EO 14389, Feb 20, 2026). Surcharge 10% (Feb 24–July 24, 2026) but 232-subject articles exempt per recital 14(k) → $0. So: 232 50% = $50,000; total $50,000 both cases.
9. June 10, 2026: 232 50% = $50,000; surcharge exempt; 301 not yet (July 24); 338 not yet (Aug 22). Total $50,000.
10. July 27, 2026: 232 50% = $50,000; 301 in effect (July 24) but exempt as 232 article (note 52(f)(1)) → $0; 338 not yet. Total $50,000.
11. Aug 25, 2026: 232 $50,000; 338 — in effect from Aug 22, but 11048 clause (2) carve-out → $0; 301 exempt → $0. Total $50,000.
12. Sept 14, 2026: same as Aug 25 → $50,000.
13. Sept 16, 2026: 232 $50,000 + 338 50% ($50,000) = $100,000 (both N and U — no USMCA exemption from section 338).
14. Nov 10, 2026: $100,000.

Also must check whether the section 338 motor-vehicles duty applies to USMCA-qualifying goods — nothing exempts them. Right.

Wait, one more: is there a "10% temporary import surcharge" stacking with 232? Recital 14(k) exempts 232 articles. Yes.

Another possible additional duty: the 2025 "reciprocal tariff" — 14257 §(e) says its rates don't apply in addition to Canada IEEPA duties; so not owed where IEEPA applied; and from Feb 20, 2026 terminated.

Also there's the section 232 copper (July 2025) — extrusions are aluminum only, all of it aluminum. Fine.

Also Q15 case U: USMCA claim → for 232 aluminum duties, is there any USMCA relief? Aluminum 232 has no USMCA exemption (except clause 2(d) in 11032 for Annex I-C products). Extrusions are Annex I-A → 50%. Fine. But hmm — the June 2026 proclamation (11032) clause (2)(d) gives Canada/Mexico USMCA treatment only for Annex I-C products. Extrusions are in Annex I-A → 50% full value.

Now, does the IEEPA exemption in EO 14231 apply to Case U? Yes: articles entered free of duty as a good of Canada under general note 11 (USMCA) are exempt.

Now Q15 asks "for each other additional duty then in force on products of Canada, say in a line why it is not owed" — so I should mention for each date: reciprocal tariff (14257), surcharge, 301, 338 as applicable.

Now Q10(f): IEEPA northern border duties: no longer in effect (EO 14389, Feb 20, 2026; published Feb 25, 2026) — and they had been in effect from March 4, 2025 (25%/10%) as amended (35% from Aug 1, 2025). The 10% temporary import surcharge: imposed for 150 days effective Feb 24, 2026 (Proc 11012), so it expired July 24, 2026 (and 232-subject articles were exempt). Therefore Canadian goods entered Sept 2026 bear neither.

Now the forced-labor section 301 memorandum (2026-15274) — need to read it to check Q14 #1 (Sept 1 deadline) and other items, plus Q9(f) (informational materials/donations). Let me read the memorandum.

content.text:
Key Q14 #1: "The memorandum gives USTR until September 1, 2026 to set up the textile tariff-rate quotas." Memorandum §2(a) says "As soon as the Trade Representative determines that it is feasible"; recital says USTR informed the President "establishing these TRQs is not feasible at this time, but that establishing these TRQs will be feasible by September 1, 2026." So statement 1 is partly correct: no deadline in the operative text; the September 1 date is a recital statement of feasibility. Good.

Also Q14 #3: seven economies moved to 10% — but note the June proposal's 10% list per the memorandum: Canada, Ecuador, EU, Indonesia, Mexico, Pakistan (imposed prohibition); Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Indonesia, Malaysia, Taiwan (ART commitments); UK (partial regime). So adopted: which moved from 12.5 to 10? Adopted 10% list = 17 economies: Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Canada, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Indonesia, Jordan, Malaysia, Mexico, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, UK, Trinidad and Tobago.

Proposal 10%: Canada, Ecuador, EU, Indonesia, Mexico, Pakistan, Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, El Salvador, Guatemala, Malaysia, Taiwan, UK. Note EU and Taiwan in proposal were 10% but adopted as 10% net of MFN (still 10% framework); adopted EU/Taiwan moved to "net" — that's the cap change.

Moved up from proposal 12.5 → adopted 10: Honduras, India, Jordan, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago = five? Hmm. Let's compute: proposal 12.5 for Honduras, India, Jordan, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago (not in the proposal 10% list). Adopted 10 for those → 5 economies. Plus Cambodia? Cambodia was in proposal 10 list (ART commitments). Guatemala also proposal 10.

But the June 5 FRN's proposal (as described in the notice at lines 164-169 and memorandum recital) had a 10% list. Hmm, statement 3 says "seven economies were moved from 12.5 percent to 10 percent because each adopted a forced-labor import ban." The documents say six economies imposed bans after June 5 (Cambodia, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago) and Jordan undertook ART commitments — seven economies total, but not all "adopted a forced-labor import ban," and of those six, Cambodia and Guatemala were already proposed at 10%. Hmm, actually were they? The memorandum recital says the proposal covered economies with ART commitments including Cambodia and Guatemala. So the ones actually moved: Honduras, India, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago (bans) and Jordan (ART) = five; Cambodia and Guatemala were already at 10 but justified now by their new bans.

Interesting. So statement 3 is partly correct: the seven economies are those that took action after June 5, but only five changed rate (Cambodia and Guatemala were already proposed at 10), and Jordan's basis was an ART commitment, not a ban.

Hmm wait. Let me double check whether the June 5 FRN proposal included Cambodia and Guatemala in the 10% list. The memorandum says 10% for: economies that "impose a forced labor import prohibition but do not yet effectively enforce it (Canada, Ecuador, EU, Indonesia, Mexico, Pakistan); have undertaken commitments in ART (Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Indonesia, Malaysia, Taiwan); or have imposed a partial regime (UK)". Yes — Cambodia and Guatemala were already proposed at 10%.

So the correct count of economies moved from 12.5 to 10 = Honduras, India, Jordan, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago = five. I should verify with the June 5 notice (2026-11296) — the proposal document itself. Let me check its list of proposed rates. That's important both for Q14 #3 and Q6(c).

Let me grep 2026-11296 for the rate list.

Also Q9(f): proposal exempted "informational materials, donations, accompanied baggage, all articles and parts of articles subject to section 232" (per notice line 170-174 and presumably the June 5 FRN). Adopted text: note 52(a) exempts "products for personal use included in accompanied baggage"; what about informational materials and donations? Let me grep 15181 for "informational" and "donation".

content.text:
Very important: 2026-11296 (June 5 proposal) at FR 34276 line 570: exemptions include "232 tariffs; USMCA-compliant goods of Canada or Mexico; and textiles and apparel... CAFTA-DR". And proposal's 10% list = 15 economies: Canada, Ecuador, EU, Indonesia, Mexico, Pakistan (imposed prohibition), Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, El Salvador, Guatemala, Indonesia, Malaysia, Taiwan (ART), UK (partial). So 10% proposed for: Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Canada, Ecuador, El Salvador, EU, Guatemala, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mexico, Pakistan, Taiwan, UK.

Adopted 10% for: Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Canada, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Indonesia, Jordan, Malaysia, Mexico, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago, UK (17). EU/Taiwan move to net-of-MFN treatment.

So economies moved from 12.5% to 10%: Honduras, India, Jordan, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago = 5. Wait but EU and Taiwan moved from "10% flat" to "10% net of MFN" — not 12.5→10.

So statement 3 ("seven economies were moved from 12.5 to 10 because each adopted a forced-labor import ban") is partly correct: seven economies are identified as having taken new action (six bans + Jordan ART), but only five actually moved from 12.5 to 10 (Honduras, India, Jordan, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago); Cambodia and Guatemala were already proposed at 10%; and Jordan's basis was an ART commitment, not a ban.

Hmm, careful: is Honduras in the proposal 10% list? No (it was one of six failing to effectively enforce, but not in the 10% list). Right, since the 10% list for "impose but not effectively enforce" includes Canada, Ecuador, EU, Indonesia, Mexico, Pakistan — not Honduras.

Now, Q13 also refers to "no program for approved onshoring plans covers it" — the June proclamation 11032 or 11021 must have such a program (the "incentive for companies to engage in..." from 11045? Actually 11045 is the aluminum proclamation establishing incentive for onshoring). Hmm, Q13 mentions "no program for approved onshoring plans covers it" — probably from Proclamation 11021 (April) which established a process for approved onshoring plans allowing reduced rates? Not needed given the assumption; but Q13(e)'s $30,000 US aluminum in a Canadian part — hmm, maybe the "85% threshold" clause (4) matters: for products with US metal ≥85% of metal weight, the rate would be 10% under (2)(c). The scenario says "most of the steel and aluminum in it, by weight, was melted or smelted outside the United States" → fails 85%.

OK. Now Q11 needs discrepancies. So far:
1. 11062 (dairy exclusion, FR 58320) clause (3) refers to a "Proclamation of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope ... With Respect to Dairy)" that does not exist — no such proclamation was issued/published. That's a statement about what another document of the same action does, differing from reality (the operative text of the series). Good.
2. 11061 (FR 58311) recital 1 says duties "effective August 19, 2026" although 11056 had amended the effective date to Aug 22 — statement about another document differing from that document's operative text as amended. Also 11076 recital 1 says "effective August 19, 2026"; and 11064/11065 recitals 1 (need to check 11064 recital 1 text — I read lines 60+; recital 1 probably says "effective August 19, 2026" too). Also 11056 recital 4/5 describe suspending "for a period of 3 days" while operative clause (1) changes the effective date rather than suspending the duties (and 11061 recital 4 says the suspension "lapsed" at Aug 22 — inconsistent with clause 1 which set a new effective date; and inconsistent with the notion that the duties never took effect until Aug 22).
3. 11056 recital 1-3 say duties imposed "effective August 19, 2026" — that's accurate when made.
4. 11046 clause (2) says duties "shall not apply to articles subject to duties pursuant to section 232" vs 11064 clause (1) "shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to section 232" — that's an amendment, not a discrepancy.
5. 11061 clause (2) refers to "Products that will be subject to the import ban ... that were imported, but not yet entered for consumption ... prior to September 29, 2026, will remain subject to the 50 percent duty rate" vs clause (1) which bans goods "imported on or after" Sept 29 — internally consistent? Clause (2) addresses goods imported before; consistent.
6. 11061 clause (3) references "the Proclamation of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope ... Alcoholic Beverages)" — that exists (11064). But note that 11061 clause (3) says the proclamation "does not otherwise affect the products ... that are subject to the additional ad valorem duties" — fine.
7. 11046 recital 9 says duties "effective as of 12:01 a.m. ... August 19, 2026" consistent.
8. 11076 recital 5 says 11065 "modified the duties imposed under Proclamation 11048" fine.
9. 11056 recital 5 says "suspending for a period of 3 days the additional ad valorem duties" while clause (1) sets effective date Aug 22 — a mismatch: the suspension described as 3-day suspension of duties vs a change of effective date. And 11061 recital 4: "the 3-day suspension ... lapsed" — implies the duties were in effect and lapsed back; operative text says the effective date was Aug 22. Hmm — this is the Q2(b) issue. Count as discrepancy? Possibly yes: 11061 recital 2 says 11056 "temporarily suspended for 3 days the effective date of the additional ad valorem duties" (suspended the effective date) — that's a slightly different characterization. Recital 4 says "the 3-day suspension ... lapsed, and the additional ad valorem duties ... became effective."

More section 301 discrepancies:
- The June 5 proposal's textile mechanism: memorandum recital says the Trade Representative proposed TRQ mechanism "to enter the United States at a zero section 301 tariff rate" (line 152: "proposed to establish a textile mechanism that would allow a certain volume of apparel and textile imports to enter the United States at a zero section 301 tariff rate") vs the June 5 FRN proposed "a reduced Section 301 tariff rate" (per notice line 158-161: "proposed a textile mechanism that would allow for a certain volume of apparel and textile imports from certain economies to enter the United States at a reduced Section 301 tariff rate"). Need to check the June 5 FRN's actual text. If the June FRN says "reduced", then the memorandum's "zero" misdescribes the proposal. Also the notice's recital (FR 47319) quoting the memorandum section 2 says TRQs allow textiles "to enter the United States free of the section 301 tariffs" — consistent with zero for the adopted directive.
- The notice's summary says "imposing tariffs on all products of the investigated economy, with certain exemptions as provided in Annexes I and II" — fine.
- Q14 #5: "Every economy whose rate is net of the MFN rate also has its own negotiated list of exempt products." Net-of-MFN economies: EU, Taiwan (10% net); Japan, Korea, Switzerland (12.5% net). Economy-specific exemption lists in note 52(j): UK (9903.05.96), EU (9903.05.97), Switzerland (9903.05.98), Malaysia, Cambodia, Guatemala, El Salvador, Argentina, Bangladesh, Taiwan, Indonesia, Ecuador, Jordan... I didn't see Japan or Korea in (j). So Japan and Korea are net-of-MFN but have no individual list in subdivision (j) — they rely on the global list (Annex I / note 52(b)). So statement 5 is incorrect (Japan and Korea).
Hmm wait — is the global exemption list note 52(b) (heading 9903.05.86, image)? Yes. Japan/Korea are covered by 9903.05.86. So incorrect.
- Q14 #7: "no product will bear more than 12.5 percent duty in total" — where might such a statement be? Perhaps in the memorandum or notice. The notice says "particularly with maximum tariffs of 12.5 percent" (FR 47334) — refers to tariff action, not total duties including MFN. And note 52(a) says products "shall also be subject to the general rates of duty imposed under subheadings in chapters 1 to 97" — so total duty = MFN + 301, e.g., 12.5% + MFN = up to more than 12.5%. And the cap in note 52(k) applies only to the listed net-of-MFN headings. So statement 7 is incorrect.
- Q14 #9 severability: correct per FR 47335.
- Q14 #8 FTZ: correct-ish; note the text says "except any product that is eligible for admission under 'domestic status'" and "only may be admitted as 'privileged foreign status,' effective as of the date that the additional duty is imposed." Statement 8 says "must be admitted in privileged foreign status, unless they are eligible for domestic status" — correct.
- Q14 #4: incorrect (FR 47331).
- Q14 #2: incorrect (over 1,600 comments, over 100 witnesses; FR 47319 and 47328; memorandum 47719).
- Q14 #6: partly correct (471 additional; sugar only "certain"/in-quota; FR 47331-47332).
- Q14 #10: correct (FR 47330: all proposed exemptions retained except non-pharmaceutical applications of certain chemical products).
- Q14 #1: partly correct (recital says feasible by Sept 1; operative §2(a) no deadline).

Additional Q11 discrepancies: maybe the notice's DATES says effective July 24, while the memorandum doesn't specify an effective date; and the notice was published July 28 (after the effective date) — not a discrepancy per se.

Maybe: The notice SUMMARY says "10 percent rate net of MFN duty" for economies meeting criteria; but the operative note 52(k) applies net treatment only to EU, Taiwan, Japan, Korea, Switzerland — consistent.

Another: notice line 490-495 (FTZ) says "effective as of the date that the additional duty is imposed" — fine.

Another: the June proposal document (11296) says 10% for economies that "impose a forced labor import prohibition but do not yet effectively enforce" — but the adopted notice's description of the proposal at line 164-168 says "proposed applying tariffs of 10 percent for each economy that imposes a forced labor import prohibition; has taken on commitments... or has imposed a partial regime" — fine.

I should check the June 5 FRN text for the textile rate ("reduced" vs "zero") and for the "12.5 percent in total" possibly appearing there. Let me grep 2026-11296 for "textile mechanism" and "zero" and "in total". Also check for statements about section 232 exemption (Q9(f)): the proposal said "all articles and parts of articles subject to tariffs under Section 232" — adopted (f) lists specific headings only. That's a substantive change, not a discrepancy (Q9(f) asks to compare).

Let me also confirm the DR exemption in proposal: "USMCA-compliant goods of Canada or Mexico" — adopted note 52(g),(h). Fine.

Now, remaining research:
1. June 5 notice (2026-11296): textile mechanism rate ("reduced" vs "zero"), and whether it proposed 12.5% for Honduras/India/Jordan/Sri Lanka/Trinidad, and any "total duties" statement. Also its DATES (proposal comment dates).
2. Proclamation 11045 (July 20, aluminum) — to ensure no change to extrusions rate (for Q15 Nov 10).
3. Q13: need to confirm "approved onshoring plans" existence (optional).
4. Q12: verify economy-specific exemption lists include the specific products for Malaysia/Cambodia/etc. (done) and the global exemption for sesame seeds (done, (c)(4)).
   - (a) Aloe etc. 1302.19.91: Cambodia → exempt (9903.06.03(C)); Malaysia → is 1302.19.91 in Malaysia's lists? Malaysia's list is 9903.05.99 (image) + 9903.06.01 particular articles: (A) psyllium, (B) boswellia, (C) argan oil — NOT aloe. So Malaysia: 10% → $6,000. Cambodia: $0.
   - (b) Boswellia 1301.90.91: Malaysia → exempt ($0); Taiwan → exempt (9903.06.15(B)) ($0); Bangladesh → 9903.06.13: (A) psyllium, (B) argan oil — no boswellia → 10% × 100,000 = $10,000; Argentina → 9903.06.11: (A) psyllium, (B) aloe..., (C) argan oil — no boswellia → 10% = $10,000.
   - (c) Argan oil 1515.90.81, MFN 4%: Taiwan → exempt ($0); Japan → not exempt; 12.5% net: 12.5-4 = 8.5% → $8,500; Indonesia → 9903.06.17: (A) aloe only — no argan → 10% flat (Indonesia is 10% flat, not net) → $10,000.
   - (d) Sesame seeds for sowing 1207.40.00, MFN 2%: globally exempt under note 52(c)(4) → $0 for Japan, Mexico, Thailand.
   - (e) Psyllium 1211.90.89: Cambodia → exempt (9903.06.03(A)) $0; Thailand → 12.5% × 40,000 = $5,000; El Salvador → exempt (9903.06.08? No — El Salvador's particular articles list (ii) has only aloe. Hmm: 9903.06.08 = aloe only for El Salvador. But psyllium might be in El Salvador's 9903.06.07 list (image) — can't tell. Hmm! For Cambodia, psyllium is listed as a "particular article"; for El Salvador only aloe. So El Salvador psyllium: 10% = $4,000? But maybe it's in the image list 9903.06.07. I must flag this uncertainty. Similarly Italy (EU): 10% net: 10-2 = 8% → $3,200; unless in EU list 9903.05.97 (image).
   - (b) Bangladesh boswellia: could be in 9903.06.12 (image) — flag uncertainty.

Given the assumption that "A product is on the annex lists the scenario names and on no other list that was published as an image" — Q12 names no annex lists, so the assumption doesn't preclude image-list membership... but it says "in any document in this task" the product is on no other list published as an image? No — that assumption applies only for lists the scenario names. Hmm, ambiguous. Safer: answer based on readable text, and flag that annex lists published as images could exempt additional products.

Actually, Q12 seems designed to test the "particular articles" lists (text) — the answer: psyllium exempt for Cambodia/Malaysia/Guatemala/Argentina/Bangladesh/Taiwan/Jordan; boswellia exempt for Malaysia/Cambodia/Guatemala/Taiwan; aloe exempt for Cambodia/Guatemala/El Salvador/Argentina/Taiwan/Indonesia/Ecuador/Jordan/Malaysia? (Malaysia's 9903.06.01 list has psyllium, boswellia, argan only); argan exempt for Malaysia/Argentina/Bangladesh/Taiwan.

So Q12 answers:
(a) Cambodia $0; Malaysia 10% = $6,000.
(b) Malaysia $0; Taiwan $0; Bangladesh $10,000; Argentina $10,000.
(c) Taiwan $0; Japan $8,500; Indonesia $10,000.
(d) all $0 (global exemption).
(e) Cambodia $0; Thailand $5,000; El Salvador $4,000 (10% flat); Italy $3,200 (8% net of 2% MFN).

Now let me verify the DR rate is 12.5% (DR in 54 list, so 12.5%) and check whether DR has any particular exemption list (note 52(j) doesn't include DR; the CAFTA-DR textile exemption (i) applies). Good.

Also Q8(a) items are not textiles, so 12.5%.

Let me now grep 2026-11296 for "textile mechanism" and "zero" to settle Q11 memo-vs-proposal discrepancy.

Confirmed: the June 5 FRN proposed "a reduced Section 301 tariff rate" (FR 34272, 34274), while the memorandum recital (2026-15274, FR 47719) says the Trade Representative "proposed to establish a textile mechanism that would allow a certain volume of apparel and textile imports to enter the United States at a zero section 301 tariff rate." That's a discrepancy (Q11).

Now, more discrepancies to find. Candidates:
(a) 11062 clause (3) referencing a nonexistent dairy scope proclamation (FR 58320).
(b) 11061 recital 1 / 11076 recital 1 (and likely 11064/11065 recitals 1) saying duties effective August 19, 2026, while 11056 amended to August 22.
(c) Memorandum "zero" vs proposal "reduced".
(d) 11056 recital 5 (suspending duties for 3 days) vs operative clause (1) (changing effective date) — and later proclamations' recital 2 ("temporarily suspended for 3 days the effective date").
(e) 11061 recital 4/11064/11065/11076 recital 4: "the 3-day suspension ... lapsed" vs 11056 clause (1) which set the effective date; and the 3 days Aug 19–21 vs Aug 22 start; actually that's consistent with "3 days". Hmm.
(f) 11061 recital 3 says "On August 21, 2026, Canada reneged" — while 11056 recital 4 said Canada expressed commitment. Not a discrepancy.
(g) In the 301 notice: SUMMARY says "with certain exemptions as provided in Annexes I and II", but the text sometimes refers to "Annex I and Annex II, Part A" etc. Not a discrepancy.
(h) The 301 notice says USTR "received over 1,600 written comments" (47319) — consistent with 47328 and memorandum 47719. Fine.
(i) In the 301 notice line 490: FTZ rule "effective as of the date that the additional duty is imposed" — while the adopted note 52 doesn't include an FTZ provision? The HTSUS note (52) as printed doesn't have an FTZ provision; the FTZ rule appears only in the preamble. Hmm, potentially a discrepancy: statement in the notice about the action vs the operative text. But not necessarily inconsistent — the FTZ rule may be in the image annex headings. Also 11046 clause (4) has an FTZ rule.
(j) Another possible 301 discrepancy: The notice says "the Trade Representative has determined to impose 10 percent tariffs on goods of ... [17 economies]" at FR 47320 (line 436-439) — but does it omit Pakistan? Let's check: line 436-439: "Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Canada, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Indonesia, Jordan, Malaysia, Mexico, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago, and the United Kingdom" — includes Pakistan. Good.
(k) The notice's section II.B determinations for individual economies: I should check a few for internal inconsistency, e.g., Taiwan/EU "except as provided in Annex I and Annex II, Part A" vs the note. Also maybe the specific economy determinations for Japan/Korea/Switzerland say "net of MFN" but reference the wrong heading. Check Japan, Korea, Switzerland, Taiwan, EU, UK, Canada entries — grep for "Japan:" etc.

Given budget (~117k), I should be judicious. Let me grep 15181 for the economy headings "Japan", "Korea", "Switzerland", "Taiwan", "European Union", "United Kingdom", "Canada", "Mexico", "Dominican Republic", "Brazil", "Türkiye", "Hong Kong", "India", "Norway", "Liechtenstein" to capture their specific determination text (needed for Q6(c) and possible discrepancies). Use pattern with colon and limit context.

content.text:
I have enough for rates:
- Japan: 12.5% net of MFN, exceptions Annex I and Annex II, Part A (so Japan has only Part A, not economy-specific Part B?). Hmm "Annex II, Part A" vs other economies referencing "Annex II, Parts A and I". E.g., Argentina "Parts A and I"; Mexico (line 953) "Parts A and E"; some "Parts A and E". So Annex II has Parts A through ... which include global (Part A) and economy-specific parts. Japan references only "Annex II, Part A" → no economy-specific list. Korea likely similar. Switzerland references "Annex II, Part..." need line 1187. So statement Q14 #5 (every net-of-MFN economy has its own negotiated list) is incorrect for Japan (and likely Korea), which reference only Annex II, Part A. But careful: the note 52(j) lists specific economy exemptions for EU, Switzerland, Taiwan, UK, Malaysia, Cambodia, Guatemala, El Salvador, Argentina, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Ecuador, Jordan — no Japan or Korea. Consistent: Japan/Korea have no economy-specific list. Good.

Also note Taiwan determination mentions "greater than or equal to 12.5 percent, the Section 301 tariff applied shall be zero"?? Wait line 1191 is within Switzerland's entry (51), saying "than or equal to 12.5 percent, the Section 301 tariff applied shall be zero." Then Taiwan entry at 1197. Hmm, line 1186-1191 is Switzerland: 12.5% net of MFN, "where such product's MFN tariff is greater than or equal to 12.5 percent, the Section 301 tariff applied shall be zero." Fine.

Now Q6(c): "For which of the ten economies in (a) does the adopted treatment differ from what was proposed in June 2026, and how? For any economy whose rate itself changed, give the reason the documents state."
Ten: Switzerland, Norway, UK, Germany(EU), Taiwan, Türkiye, Japan, Liechtenstein, Hong Kong, India.
- Switzerland: proposed 12.5% flat; adopted 12.5% net of MFN → differs (cap).
- Norway: same 12.5% flat → no change.
- UK: 10% both → no change.
- Germany/EU: proposed 10% flat; adopted 10% net of MFN → differs.
- Taiwan: proposed 10% flat; adopted 10% net → differs.
- Türkiye: 12.5% both → no change.
- Japan: proposed 12.5% flat; adopted 12.5% net → differs.
- Liechtenstein: not investigated (not among the 60) → no duty; no change (never proposed).
- Hong Kong: 12.5% both.
- India: proposed 12.5%; adopted 10% → changed, reason: India adopted a forced labor import prohibition after June 5, 2026 (notice FR 47324, line 823-826; memorandum recital FR 47720).

Wait — was Japan proposed at 12.5% flat? Yes (Japan in 54 list, not in proposal 10% list). Adopted 12.5% net. Korea similarly. So four economies got net-of-MFN treatment (EU, Taiwan at 10%; Japan, Korea, Switzerland at 12.5%) — five total.

Now Q6(b) fine.

Now, remaining: Proclamation 11045 (July 20 aluminum) — check if it changes rates for aluminum articles. Let me grep for "50 percent"/"Sec"/"clause (1)".

Also need to double-check the dairy scope proclamation nonexistence: search fr_search for "Dairy" presdocu 2026 in Sept — earlier search showed no dairy scope modification. Good. Maybe also search full text "Modifying the Scope ... Dairy" to be safe (could be a doc published later). Let me do a quick search: query "Modifying the Scope of Products of Canada ... Dairy" doc_type PRESDOCU.

Also to answer Q1's "which documents changed which products" for dairy: only 11047 (impose) and 11062 (exclusion).

Let me also confirm 11047 clause numbering/rate consistent and its citation 91 FR 46653; 11048 91 FR 46663.

One more needed: Q3(b) FTZ — Actually 11061 has no FTZ provision, so rely on 11046 clause (4). Fine.

Also Q1 asks "the date signed, the date published" for each — I have those.

Also Q5(b) asks filing date for Oct scope: "Filed 10-29-26; 11:15 am" → filed Oct 29; published Oct 30. Good.

Let me do the 11045 grep and a search to confirm no dairy scope doc.

Confirmed: no dairy scope modification exists; only 11062 references it. 

11045 (July 20, 2026): establishes aluminum onshoring plans program (half the 232 rate) — no rate change for extrusions absent approval. Q13's assumption "no program for approved onshoring plans covers it" aligns.

Now I have most needed. Remaining gaps:
1. Q2/Q1: Does any document specify the "date and time from which operative change applies" for 11056 measured against? 11056 clause (1): "The effective date of the additional ad valorem duties ... shall be 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 22, 2026" — measured against the effective date of the duties (entry/withdrawal per clauses 1/3 of the base proclamations and annex chapeaux).
2. Q2(d): "Did the duties need a further presidential action in order to begin? What do later documents say happened in the days before they began?" Covered.
3. Q3/Q10: fine.
4. Q9(f): proposal said exemptions for informational materials, donations, accompanied baggage, all 232 articles (per notice FR 47318-47319; need the June 5 FRN language — line 570 mentions "232 tariffs; USMCA-compliant goods of Canada or Mexico; and textiles..."). Let me get the June FRN's exemption list sentence (around line 560-575 of 11296) for accurate citation. I'll grep 11296 for "informational materials".

5. Q15: need the CIT/other? No.

6. Q16? No, 15 questions.

7. Q11: I want a couple more discrepancies. Let me think about the 301 notice vs memorandum:
- Memorandum §1(a)(i) lists 17 economies at 10%: includes Pakistan. The notice's recital (line 436) lists the same 17. OK.
- Memorandum recital says proposal included 10% for "Canada, Ecuador, the European Union, Indonesia, Mexico, and Pakistan" (impose but not effectively enforce). The June 5 FRN's list — need to confirm it included the same six. Grep 11296 lines 300-340.
- The notice §II.B for individual economies: e.g., India's determination cites India's adoption of a prohibition; consistent.
- Possible discrepancy: Notice line 490-495 FTZ rule says "effective as of the date that the additional duty is imposed" — but the duties are imposed effective July 24, i.e., before the notice was published (July 28); fine.
- Another possible: The notice at 47319 says "USTR received over 1,600 written comments" and at 47328 "over 1,600 written comments and heard testimony from over 100 witnesses" — consistent.
- Another: The notice's DATES: in-transit exception applies to goods "entered ... before 12:01 a.m. ... July 28, 2026". Fine.
- Another: 2026-11296 proposal line 570: exemptions for "232 tariffs; USMCA-compliant goods of Canada or Mexico" — but the adopted text exempts only specific 232 headings (not all 232 articles). Q9(f) covers it as a change, not discrepancy.
- Potential discrepancy: The memorandum recital says the June 5 FRN "proposed ... imposing ad valorem tariffs on all goods of each investigated economy" — consistent.
- Potential discrepancy: the June 5 FRN summary says it proposes "10%" for economies that impose a prohibition etc. Also says "The Trade Representative also proposes a textile mechanism ... at a reduced Section 301 tariff rate." The memorandum says "zero". Already have.
- Potential discrepancy in 11061: recital 5 says Saskatchewan "is one of two provinces that at the time of the signing of Proclamation 11046 ... did not outright ban U.S. alcoholic beverages" — vs 11046 recital 4 which says "Only the provinces of Alberta and Saskatchewan subsequently lifted their bans ... in June 2025" — consistent.
- 11056: recital 4 says officials recommend suspending "for a period of 3 days the additional duties"; clause (1) changes the effective date. Recital 5 same. So a statement in one document (11056 recitals) about what the action provides vs its operative text (a 3-day suspension of duties vs a change of effective date). Hmm, could be framed as internal inconsistency: recitals say duties are "suspended" for 3 days, but the operative text provides that the duties' effective date is Aug 22 — meaning they never took effect on Aug 19 and thus there was nothing to suspend; later proclamations describe it both ways ("suspended for 3 days the effective date" (recital 2) and "the 3-day suspension lapsed, and the ... duties ... became effective" (recital 4)). Good discrepancy.
- Bigger: 11061 recital 1 and 11076 recital 1 say duties were "effective August 19, 2026," though the documents' operative text (as amended by 11056) makes them effective Aug 22. Also 11064 recital 1? Let me check 11064 lines 1-60 (I skipped recital 1). Also 11062 recital 1 and 11063/11065.

Let me grep 11064/11062/11063/11065 for "August 19".

10. Q6(a)(8) Liechtenstein: confirm not among 60 investigated economies — the memorandum list of 60 doesn't include Liechtenstein. Good. But wait — Liechtenstein is in the 232 proclamation's EU-like list; irrelevant. So no section 301 duty for Liechtenstein (not investigated). Note uncertainty: no 301 action.

Informational materials and donations: not mentioned in the adopted note text I read — but they may be in the image lists (note 52(b) heading 9903.05.86 list). Hmm. Q9(f) asks: what did the proposal say about goods subject to section 232 duties, and about informational materials and donations? What does the adopted text say on each?

Adopted text: (f) exempts articles of aluminum/steel/copper and derivative articles in specific headings (9903.82.02, .04-.26), passenger vehicles, parts, wood, MHDVs, semiconductor articles, patented pharmaceuticals (added July 31) — a closed list of headings, not "all articles subject to 232 tariffs." For informational materials and donations: the adopted note text doesn't state a general exemption in the readable text; whether they're in the image annex lists (Annex I/II) can't be verified. Hmm, but the notice's Annex I A includes the note 52; and Annex II lists. Since the adopted rule text doesn't mention them, I should say: the adopted text as printed does not contain any general exemption for informational materials or donations; they are not mentioned in note 52's subdivisions (a)-(k), though Annex I/II lists published as images may cover specific HTS provisions (e.g., books under 4901). Flag uncertainty.

Now let me check 11064 recital 1 for "August 19" (the doc number for 11064 is 2026-18838, not 18863 — my grep used a wrong number "2026-18863" which exists?! It returned 220 lines — odd. Whatever, wrong doc.)

Let me grep 2026-18838 and 2026-18837 (MV exclusion) for "August 19".
