content.text:
Confirmed: all the later proclamations (11061, 11062, 11063, 11064, 11065, 11076) recite "effective August 19, 2026" in their first recital, which conflicts with the amended operative text (Aug 22).

Now the dairy exclusion 11062 clause (2) says "remain subject to the 50 percent duty rate established by Proclamation 11047" — fine.

I think I have enough for a comprehensive answer. Some remaining items worth a quick check:

A. Q1 asks for FR citation first page for each — have.
B. Q1 "one line on what it does" — have.
C. Q1 "Say which kind of event that date and time is measured against in each document" — have.

D. Q5(a) times: 3:00 p.m. Sept 14; 12:01 a.m. Sept 15; 4:00 p.m. Oct 29; 12:01 a.m. Oct 30; Nov 3 — Have.

E. Q9(d): Japanese passenger car under 232 heading 9903.94.01 → exempt under (f)(2). $0. Note also 232-related.

F. Q9(e): Brazil 232 duty under a chapter 99 heading not mentioned → 12.5%.

G. Q8(c): dates: signed July 23, 2026; applies from 12:01 a.m. ET July 24; published July 28.

H. Q10(f): IEEPA and surcharge — done.

I. Q15: need to double check the 2025 dates: Mar 6, 2025 — IEEPA in effect from March 4, 2025 at 12:01 a.m. (EO 14197). And EO 14231 (Mar 6) effective March 7, 2025 (12:01 a.m. EST March 7) providing USMCA exemption and potash 10%. So on March 6, is the USMCA exemption in effect? EO 14231 says modifications effective March 7, 2025. So on March 6, no USMCA exemption → Case U pays 25% on Mar 6! Good catch. Let me confirm EO 14231's effective date: clause (c): "The modifications set out in this section shall be effective with respect to goods entered ... on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern standard time on March 7, 2025." Yes (FR 11785). So:
- Mar 6, 2025: Case U also subject to 25% IEEPA (no USMCA carve-out yet) → total $35,000 both cases.
- Mar 10, 2025: Case U exempt (25% not owed) → $10,000 (232 at 10%).
Good — that's a designed distinction.

J. Q15 case U for 232: no USMCA relief for aluminum articles in Annex I-A in 2025/2026 (11032 clause 2(d) applies to Annex I-C). So 232 full 50%/25%/10% in both cases.

K. Q15 date 1 (Feb 10, 2025): 232 10% (before Mar 12, 2025). IEEPA not yet in effect (Feb 4 date postponed to Mar 4 by EO 14197). Also reciprocal not yet. So Case N = $10,000, Case U = $10,000.

L. Q15 date 8 (Mar 2, 2026): IEEPA terminated Feb 20, 2026 (EO 14389) — "shall no longer be in effect and, as soon as practicable, no longer collected". Surcharge from Feb 24, 2026 — 10%, but 232-subject articles exempt (recital 14(k)). So total = 232 50% = $50,000.

Hmm wait: is the surcharge's 232 exemption operative text or recital? It's in the recital (para 14) with "as further detailed in Annexes I and II". The operative clauses may also say. For robustness, cite recital 14(k) and note the annexes are images. Alternatively the extrusions are aluminum articles and likely in Annex I/II exemption lists. Q15 assumption: "no exemption exists other than those readable as text" — hmm, that says assumptions include "no exemption exists other than those readable as text." That might mean the surcharge's 232 exemption (readable) applies. Yes — recital 14(k) is readable text, so exemption applies.

Similarly for the section 301 232 exemption (note 52(f)(1) lists headings 9903.82.02 — readable). Good.

M. Q15 date 14 (Nov 10, 2026): 232 50% + 338 50% (no USMCA relief) = $100,000.

N. Q13 (c): Canada no USMCA → 25% of full $200,000 = $50,000.

O. Q13 (a): 25% of non-US content ($140,000) = $35,000; floor 15% of $200,000 = $30,000 → $35,000.
(g): 25% of $60,000 = $15,000 → below floor → $30,000.

Hmm, "total effective duty on the imported product assessed under this subclause shall not be less than 15 percent ad valorem" — 15% of the customs value = $30,000. Yes.

P. Q13 (h): after Dec 31, 2027 → rates in clause (3) of Proclamation 11021 (Jan 1, 2028). I don't know the clause (3) rates — could state they're the generally applicable rates set in Proclamation 11021 clause (3) (FR 18201), which I haven't read in detail. Let me quickly grep 11021 for "clause (3)" rates: from earlier grep, clause (3) of 11021 covers copper articles and aluminum/steel derivative articles in Annex I-B at 25%/15%/... Hmm — clause (3) of 11021 sets 25% for Annex I-B derivative articles. So after 2028, the Annex I-C products revert to the rates in 11021 clause (3) — 25% (with 15% UK, 25% non-normal-trade). I can state: 25 percent (with the lower rates specified in that clause), citing 11032 clause (3)(a) and 11021 clause (3)(a). Let me be careful: 11021 clause (3) covers "copper articles and ... aluminum and steel derivative articles listed in Annex I-B" → 25%. And the mobile industrial machine is a steel article in Annex I-C (a derivative). So after Jan 1, 2028, 25% under 11021 clause (3)(a). Reasonable.

Q. Q11: I should also look for discrepancies within the 301 notice: e.g., the SUMMARY says "with specific economies subject to a 10 percent rate net of a product's MFN duty" — the operative text also applies 12.5% net for Japan/Korea/Switzerland; consistent.

Maybe the notice's statement at line 1997-2011 about "The President has directed ... Exemptions directed by the President are limited to ... (5) products that if exempted ..." — fine.

Maybe: the notice at 47319 says the June 5 FRN "proposed applying tariffs of 10 percent for each economy that imposes a forced labor import prohibition..." — but the June FRN says 10% for economies that "impose a forced labor import prohibition but do not yet effectively enforce it" (per memorandum recital FR 47719). Minor.

Another potential discrepancy: Notice at FR 47321 (line 434-440) says "impose a tariff of 10 percent on goods of Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Canada, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Indonesia, Jordan, Malaysia, Mexico, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago, and the United Kingdom" — but the SUMMARY (FR 47318) list of criteria... fine.

Perhaps a real discrepancy: The June 5 FRN's proposed exemption said "all articles and parts of articles that are subject to section 232 tariffs" while the adopted note 52(f) exempts only listed headings — that's a change, and Q9(f) covers it. But is there a document that *describes* the adopted action as exempting all 232 articles (inaccurate description)? The notice at FR 47319 line 170-174 describes the June 5 proposal accurately. Hmm. Maybe the notice's response to comments at FR 47334 line 2030: "many inputs, including auto parts already subject to Section 232 tariffs, are exempt from additional tariffs pursuant to this action" — that's an accurate statement re listed auto parts.

Another: the notice's section III.E says "The President has directed the Trade Representative to impose tariffs on all goods of the 60 investigated economies" — consistent.

Another candidate discrepancy: 11046 clause (2) says duties "shall not apply to articles subject to duties pursuant to section 232" and clause (1) imposes 50% on Annex II products without regard to 232; the annex chapeau might include a carve-out. Not verifiable.

Another candidate: 11056's recital 4 says officials opined "the public interests favor suspending for a period of 3 days the additional duties" — but the actual period from Aug 19 to Aug 22 is 3 days. Fine.

Another: 11061 clause (2) says products "imported, but not yet entered for consumption ... prior to September 29, 2026, will remain subject to the 50 percent duty rate established by Proclamation 11046" — this implies that goods imported before Sept 29 but entered after remain dutiable, consistent with clause (1)'s "imported on or after" test. But there's tension with 11046 clause (1) which measures duty by entry, not importation. Not a discrepancy between documents though.

Another discrepancy candidate: 11062 clause (3) says the Sept 8 dairy scope proclamation — nonexistent (strong).
Also: 11061 clause (3) refers to the Sept 8 alcoholic scope proclamation by name — exists. But 11062's parallel reference is to a nonexistent doc — discrepancy.

Another: 11063 (MV exclusion) clause (3) references a Sept 8 MV scope proclamation — exists (11065).

Another: 11076 recital 5 says 11065 "modified the duties imposed under Proclamation 11048 after receiving certain information..." fine.

Another discrepancy: 11076 recital 1 says duties "effective August 19, 2026" (already counted, list once with all docs).

Another: In 11056 recital 1-3, it says "I imposed ... additional ad valorem duties, effective August 19, 2026" — accurate as of that date.

Another: Q11 also asks about the section 301 action's documents disagreeing "with themselves". Options:
- Notice SUMMARY says "imposing tariffs on all products of the investigated economy, with certain exemptions as provided in Annexes I and II" but the operative note applies tariffs only under headings 9903.05.20-9903.05.84 and note 52(a) says "except as provided in headings 9903.05.85-9903.06.21" — fine.
- The notice at 47321 states the FTZ rule: "Any product ... admitted into a U.S. foreign trade zone ... only may be admitted as privileged foreign status ... effective as of the date that the additional duty is imposed." But the operative note 52 (as printed) contains no FTZ provision (subdivisions (a)-(k) don't address FTZ; the FTZ requirement would be in the image annex headings perhaps). Could flag as a possible discrepancy but risky (may be in the image). Skip or mention cautiously? Q11 says don't list matters where a document is merely silent. So skip.
- The notice's statement in section III.E (FR 47334): "maximum tariffs of 12.5 percent" — vs operative text where tariffs can be 12.5% plus MFN; but that's not inconsistent — the 301 tariff max is 12.5%.
- The memorandum: "Section 1(a)(i) 10 percent tariff rate ... on goods of [17]" and the notice's recital list matches.
- The memorandum §2(c): "Until the TRQs are established, the Trade Representative shall impose the applicable section 301 tariffs provided for in section 1(a) ... (here, 10 percent) on imports of specific textile and apparel of Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, and Malaysia that will be covered by the TRQs" — but the notice says the TRQ mechanism will be established in a separate notice, and doesn't implement §2(c). Not necessarily a discrepancy.
- Possibly: The June 5 FRN said textile mechanism at "reduced" rate; memorandum says "zero"; the notice (quoting the memorandum at FR 47319 section 2) says TRQs allow textiles "to enter the United States free of the section 301 tariffs" — so the notice and memorandum describe the directive as zero-based, while the proposal said reduced. That's the same discrepancy (list once: memo vs proposal).

Hmm, another possible: The June 5 FRN proposed 10% for the EU (a member-state group) and Taiwan; the memorandum recital says the proposal gave 10% for ART-committing economies including Taiwan, and for those imposing a prohibition (EU). Adopted: EU/Taiwan 10% net. Fine.

One more potential discrepancy: The notice's §II.B(3) Argentina says "10 percent tariffs on products of Argentina, except as provided in Annex I and Annex II, Parts A and I" — Parts A and I? Odd part labels. Skip.

I'd like at least 4-6 discrepancies. Let me also consider the section 338 series' other internal inconsistency: 11046 clause (2) says the duties "are in addition to any other duties..." and "shall not apply to articles subject to duties pursuant to section 232"; 11064 clause (1) says the duties "shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to section 232" — but 11064 clause (1) also says products in Part B "shall no longer be subject to the additional ad valorem duty" — consistent.

Another: 11056 clause (1) amends only "the chapeau of Annex II" — but the operative clauses remain inconsistent → that's Q2(b). As a discrepancy for Q11: 11056 operative clause (1) sets the effective date as Aug 22 while 11046's operative clauses (1) and (3) still print Aug 19 — a difference between documents of the same action; but that's an amendment by amendment of annex only, so it's arguably a discrepancy: 11056 says "the effective date ... shall be August 22" and amends only the annex chapeau, leaving contrary text in the clauses. I can list it (as a discrepancy between 11056's operative text and the unamended operative text of 11046).

Q: Does 11061 recital 2's statement match 11056? "I temporarily suspended for 3 days the effective date" — 11056 clause 1 did not use "suspend"; it changed the effective date. Minor.

Also potentially: 11061 recital 4 says the duties "became effective" at Aug 22 because the suspension "lapsed"; but 11056's text made Aug 22 the effective date regardless of lapse; and the later documents also say Canada reneged on Aug 21 — after the amendment. But the rate would have become effective Aug 22 even had Canada complied (since 11056 set Aug 22 as the effective date, with no provision extending it). Not exactly a discrepancy.

Another good discrepancy: 11062 clause (2) says goods "will remain subject to the 50 percent duty rate established by Proclamation 11047" — but the dairy exemption's clause (1) bans importation of goods "imported on or after" Sept 29; for goods imported before but entered after, fine.

I think I have enough. But let me search the 301 notice for statements about "no product" / "in total" / "stack" to see if some document says total duties won't exceed 12.5%, which would be a discrepancy vs note 52(a) (which stacks MFN). Grep for "in total" and "stack".

Also Q14 #7 needs the deciding passages: note 52(a) ("shall also be subject to the general rates of duty") and note 52(k) cap (only net-of-MFN headings), plus notice FR 47334 ("maximum tariffs of 12.5 percent" refers to the section 301 tariffs).

Let me do a couple final greps: "in total" in 15181 and 15274; and "total" in 15274.

Budget ~109k. Fine.

content.text:
Good. Now, I should verify one Q9 item: (c)(i) Mexico USMCA-free → exempt under note 52(h) (heading 9903.05.94). Yes.

Also Q9(a): Thailand rate — Thailand is 12.5% (in 54 list, not 10%). Yes.

Q9(b): Israel 12.5%.

Now, Q6(a)(8) Liechtenstein: Not investigated → no action. Good.

Let me also double check the "certain particular articles" exemption heading for Malaysia: 9903.06.01 covers "the following particular articles the product of Malaysia: (A) psyllium, (B) boswellia, (C) argan oil" — and the duty imposed by heading 9903.05.54 doesn't apply. Good.

Now, one more thing for Q12(a): Cambodia's heading is 9903.05.28 (10%) and exemption 9903.06.03 includes aloe (1302.19.91) → $0.

Q12(c) Japan: is argan oil exempt for Japan? No economy-specific list (Japan references Annex II Part A only) → 8.5%.

Q12(d): sesame seeds for sowing exempt globally under note 52(c)(4) via heading 9903.05.87. Note: the exemption is for "Sesame seeds, whether or not broken, for sowing (1207.40.00)". Scenario says "sesame seeds for sowing (subheading 1207.40.00)" → exempt. $0.

Q12(e) El Salvador psyllium: (ii) list has only aloe; so 10% ($4,000), but flag possible image-list coverage.
Italy (EU) psyllium: 10% net of 2% → 8% = $3,200; EU-specific list 9903.05.97 is an image → flag.

Now let me consider Q2(c) more carefully: "On entry 1 the broker deposited the 50 percent duty. What do the documents say about getting it back?" Documents: 11056 clause (2) directs agencies to "suspend the collection of the additional ad valorem duties ... to the extent required"; clause (4): "To the extent that implementation of this proclamation requires a refund of duties collected, refunds shall be processed pursuant to applicable law and CBP's standard procedures for such refunds." No interest provision; no form specified. Also 11046's clauses don't address refunds. And 11061 doesn't address refunds of duties paid on Aug 19-21. So answer: refund available per 11056 clause (4).

Now, Q2(a) arithmetic: $40,000 × 50% = $20,000; entries 1 and 2 → $0 (before effective date), entry 3 → $20,000. Note entry 3 at exactly 12:01 a.m. Aug 22 → "on or after" → applies.

Also note: wine is subject to... any 232? No.

Q4(c) exact text with FR page:
- 11046 clause (2), FR 46641: "The duties imposed in this proclamation shall not apply to articles subject to duties pursuant to section 232..."
- 11064 clause (1), FR 58332: "The duties imposed pursuant to Proclamation 11046, as modified in this proclamation, shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to section 232..."
- 11047 clause (2), FR 46655 (dairy): same carve-out. Need exact FR page for 11047's clause (2): grep showed FR page 46655 for lines 193-197. Yes 91 FR 46655.
- 11065 clause (1), FR 58340.

Q5(b): Note also that these scope proclamations do not have retroactive effect: 11065 clause (1)-(2) apply to goods entered on/after Sept 15; 11076 clauses (1)-(2) apply to entries on/after Oct 30; no refund provisions in either (contrast 11056 clause (4)). And 11064 clause (1)-(2) similar.

Q5(c): P: signed Sept 8 → dutiable Sept 15 (7 days); S: signed Oct 23 → dutiable Oct 30 (7 days). The scope proclamations recite the 30-day limit (11065 recital 8, FR 58340; 11076 recital 9, FR 68862) but never explain how a 7-day effective date is consistent; they characterize the action as modifying the scope of already-imposed duties (11065 recital 6-7; 11076 recital 7-8), and the original 30-day period ran from the July 20, 2026 finding (duties effective Aug 22). No explanation of the waiting period for newly covered products.

Q1: also mention 11045? No — that's section 232, not section 338.

Also Q1: "List every presidential document in the section 338 series against Canada published through today." That's 10 documents (11046, 11047, 11048, 11056, 11061-11065, 11076).

Now Q13(h): "Until when does the treatment in (a) apply, and what applies afterwards?" Clause (2) applies through Dec 31, 2027 (11:59 p.m. EST); from Jan 1, 2028, clause (3)(a) sets rates in clause (3) of Proclamation 11021 (25% for Annex I-B derivative articles etc.). I should double-check 11021 clause (3) rates: from grep, clause (3) covers copper articles and aluminum/steel derivative articles in Annex I-B: "(a) 25 percent, unless lower applies pursuant to (3)(b)-(3)(c)". So say 25% (with the lower UK rate), citing 11021 clause (3)(a).

Hmm — but is the mobile industrial machine in Annex I-B or I-C? Q13 says it's in Annex I-C of the June proclamation. After 2028, 11032 clause (3)(a) says rates "set out in clause (3) of Proclamation 11021" — so 25%.

Also Q13(f): same as (e) — nothing in the documents changes between Oct 6 and Oct 20, 2026 for 232. I'll say $45,000 (same), and note why.

Q2.answer:
(a) All three entries are of the same Annex II wine ($40,000 customs value, 50% rate). The controlling text is cl. (1) of Proclamation 11046 as amended by cl. (1) of Proclamation 11056: the duty applies "effective for goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 22, 2026."
- Entry 1 (Aug. 20, 2:00 p.m.): before the effective time → **$0**. ($40,000 × 50% = $20,000, but the duty does not yet apply.)
- Entry 2 (Aug. 21, 11:59 p.m.): one minute before the effective time → **$0**.
- Entry 3 (Aug. 22, 12:01 a.m.): at the effective time, and "on or after" includes that instant → 50% × $40,000 = **$20,000**.

(b) Proclamation 11056 cl. (1) (91 FR 54790) states: "The effective date of the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamations 11046, 11047, and 11048 shall be 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 22, 2026," and then amends **only** "the chapeau of Annex II of each of Proclamations 11046, 11047, and 11048" by deleting "August 19, 2026" and inserting "August 22, 2026." What was **not** amended: the operative clauses of the three base proclamations — cl. (1) and cl. (3) of 11046 (91 FR 46641), and their counterparts in 11047 (46654–46655) and 11048 (46665) — which still print "August 19, 2026." The difference is resolved by the later, specific operative direction in 11056 cl. (1) itself (the effective date "shall be" Aug. 22), reinforced by 11056 cl. (5) (inconsistent earlier provisions superseded to the extent of inconsistency, 91 FR 54791) and by the later proclamations, which state that "at 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 22, 2026, the 3-day suspension imposed by Proclamation 11056 lapsed, and the additional ad valorem duties imposed under Proclamation 11046 became effective" (11061 recital 4, 91 FR 58311; same recital 4 in 11064 at 58331, 11065 at 58339, 11076 at 68861).

(c) Proclamation 11056 cl. (4) (91 FR 54791): "To the extent that implementation of this proclamation requires a refund of duties collected, refunds shall be processed pursuant to applicable law and CBP's standard procedures for such refunds." Clause (2) also directed agencies to "as soon as practicable, suspend the collection of the additional ad valorem duties" (91 FR 54790). No document states an interest entitlement, a protest right, or a specific refund form; none addresses refunds of amounts deposited for Aug. 19–21 entries other than through cl. (4).

(d) No further presidential action was needed. 11061 recital 4 (91 FR 58311) and the identical recitals in 11064/11065/11076 state that the duties "became effective" automatically when the 3-day suspension lapsed at 12:01 a.m. on Aug. 22. As to the days before: 11056 recital 4 (54790) records Canada's expressed commitment to remove the discrimination; the later proclamations state that "[o]n August 21, 2026, Canada reneged on its commitment, ceased negotiating in good faith, and did not remove the discrimination" (11061 recital 3, 91 FR 58311; 11064 recital 3, 58331; 11065 recital 3, 58339; 11076 recital 3, 68861), and 11061 recital 5 adds Saskatchewan's Aug. 27, 2026 announced 50% levy.

(e) Recital 10 of 11046 (91 FR 46640–46641) quotes section 338: duties may "not … take effect earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation" finding the discrimination. Proclamation 11046 was signed July 20, 2026 (91 FR 46639). Arithmetic: July 20 + 30 days = **August 19, 2026**; hence recital 9 (46639) and cl. (1) fixed "12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 19, 2026" — the earliest lawful moment. (The amended date, Aug. 22, is 33 days after signing and so also satisfies the 30-day minimum.)
Q2.uncertainty: The text does not say which entry date governs for goods entered exactly at 12:01 a.m.; the "on or after" wording is read literally. The documents do not say whether a refund under 11056 cl. (4) carries interest, and they do not describe any procedure beyond "CBP's standard procedures."

Q3.answer:
The beer is dutiable under 11046 (Annex II), was not removed by 11064, and is on the Annex to 11061. The ban in 11061 cl. (1) applies to goods **imported on or after 12:01 a.m. ET Sept. 29, 2026**; cl. (2) keeps the 50% duty on goods imported before that time but not yet entered or withdrawn (91 FR 58312). Value $30,000; 50% = $15,000 per shipment.

(a)
- **A** (arrives Sept. 10; entered Sept. 14): imported before Sept. 29 and entered before Sept. 29 → may be imported; duty 50% × $30,000 = **$15,000** (11046 cl. (1) as amended).
- **B** (arrives Sept. 27; bonded warehouse; withdrawn Oct. 5): imported before Sept. 29, so not banned; cl. (2) of 11061 keeps it "subject to the 50 percent duty rate established by Proclamation 11046" → **$15,000** on the Oct. 5 withdrawal.
- **C** (arrives 11:30 p.m. Sept. 28; entry 9:00 a.m. Sept. 29): imported before Sept. 29 → not banned; it was "imported, but not yet entered for consumption … prior to September 29, 2026," so cl. (2) applies → **$15,000**.
- **D** (arrives 12:30 a.m. Sept. 29): imported on/after the effective time → **excluded from importation**; no consumption entry may be made. No section 338 duty arises because there is no lawful importation (the duty is replaced by the ban).

(b) **E** (arrives Sept. 25; admitted to an FTZ Sept. 25; entry for consumption from the zone Oct. 6): because it was admitted to the zone after the Aug. 22 effective date, 11046 cl. (4) (91 FR 46641) requires admission in "privileged foreign status" (unless domestic status applies), and on entry for consumption it is subject to the ad valorem rate for its heading. On the exclusion side, E was imported before Sept. 29, so 11061 cl. (2) applies: it "will remain subject to the 50 percent duty rate" → **50% × $30,000 = $15,000**, and no import ban.

(c) If a court invalidates the import ban as applied to this beer, 11061 cl. (9)(b) (91 FR 58313) provides that "the 50 percent ad valorem duty imposed in Proclamation 11046 shall apply to the import to which the invalidated import ban … had applied before its invalidation." So later shipments of the beer would be importable and dutiable at **50%** under Proclamation 11046.

(d) No. 11061 cl. (3) (91 FR 58312) states that, besides converting listed products from duty to ban, "this proclamation does not otherwise affect the products, as further established in the Proclamation of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope … With Respect to Alcoholic Beverages), that are subject to the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11046." Listed Canadian alcoholic products not in the Annex therefore remain subject to the 50% duty as modified by 11064.
Q3.uncertainty: The documents nowhere address the treatment of goods held in a foreign trade zone when the ban's effective date passes; the outcome in (b) rests on 11061 cl. (2)'s "imported, but not yet entered" rule plus 11046 cl. (4), and would be different if "imported" were read to mean the customs entry rather than arrival. For (d) the text is clear; for (c) the text does not say whether the 50% duty applies retroactively to goods denied entry while the ban was in force.

(a) 50% duty applies as follows (yes = 50% duty applies):

|---|---|---|---|---|

| Nov. 3 | **Yes** | No | No | **Yes** |

Bases: P became subject when 11065 cl. (1) took effect for entries on/after 12:01 a.m. ET Sept. 15, 2026 (91 FR 58340). Q was dutiable under 11048 from Aug. 22 and was removed by 11065 Annex I, Part B, also effective Sept. 15 (same clause). R was dutiable from Aug. 22 and was removed by 11076 Annex I, Part A, effective 12:01 a.m. ET Oct. 30, 2026 (91 FR 68862) — so it is still dutiable on Oct. 29 at 4:00 p.m. S became subject only when 11076 Annex I, Part B took effect at 12:01 a.m. Oct. 30 (same clause).

(b) Proclamation 11076: **signed October 23, 2026**; **filed with the Office of the Federal Register October 29, 2026** (closing line "Filed 10-29-26; 11:15 am"); **published October 30, 2026** at 91 FR 68861. It applies from **12:01 a.m. ET October 30, 2026** to goods "entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption" (cl. (1)–(2), 91 FR 68862). The scope proclamations do **not** reach earlier entries: both 11065 and 11076 are expressly limited to entries/withdrawals on or after their effective times, and neither contains any retroactivity, refund or retroactive-relief provision (compare 11056 cl. (4), 91 FR 54791, which does address refunds).

(c) Section 338's waiting period is quoted in each scope proclamation: duties may "not … take effect earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation" (11065 recital 8, 91 FR 58340; 11076 recital 9, 91 FR 68862). P became dutiable **7 days** after signing (Sept. 8 → Sept. 15); S became dutiable **7 days** after signing (Oct. 23 → Oct. 30). Neither proclamation explains how a 7-day effective date fits the 30-day period. They characterize the action only as "modifying the scope of products" already subject to section 338 duties imposed after the July 20, 2026 finding (11065 recitals 6–7, 58340; 11076 recitals 7–8, 68862); no recital states that the 30-day clock ran from the July 20, 2026 proclamation or otherwise addresses the waiting period for newly covered products.
Q5.uncertainty: Whether a scope modification that adds products is a "new duty" subject to the 30-day waiting period is not addressed anywhere in the text; the proclamations are silent, and no amendment of section 338 is published in these documents.

Q7.answer:
(a) France (EU, 10% net of MFN). MFN duty: 3¢ × 2,000 kg = $60. Ad valorem equivalent = $60 ÷ $12,000 = **0.5%**. Section 301 = 10% − 0.5% = 9.5% → 0.095 × $12,000 = **$1,140**.

(b) MFN: 4% × $20,000 = $800, plus 25¢ × 4,000 kg = $1,000 → **$1,800**; AVE = $1,800 ÷ $20,000 = **9%**.
- **Italy (EU)**: 10% − 9% = 1% → **$200**.
- **Japan**: 12.5% − 9% = 3.5% → **$700**.
- **Brazil**: 12.5% flat → **$2,500**.

(c) MFN = $2,200 ÷ $20,000 = **11%**.
- **Taiwan**: at or above 10% → section 301 = **$0**.
- **Switzerland**: below 12.5% → 12.5% − 11% = 1.5% → **$300**.

(d) The rule is in U.S. note 52(k) to subchapter III of chapter 99, HTSUS, added by Annex I to the USTR notice at **91 FR 47394**: "for any good of a member state of the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland or Taiwan subject to a specific or compound rate of duty under column 1-General, the ad valorem equivalent rate of duty … shall be determined by dividing the amount of duty payable under column 1-General by the customs value of the good" (with a worked example of 50¢/kg on a $10/kg good = 5%). The result where the equivalent rate is at or above the cap appears in the same subdivision (91 FR 47394): "For headings 9903.05.39 and 9903.05.76, articles for which the applicable column 1 duty rate is less than 10 percent, the sum of the column 1 duty rate and the additional ad valorem rate of duty is 10 percent"; "For headings 9903.05.49, 9903.05.71 and 9903.05.74, articles for which the applicable column 1 duty rate is less than 12.5 percent, the sum … is 12.5 percent" — and the zero-at-or-above-the-cap result is stated in the memorandum §1(a)(ii) (91 FR 47720) and the notice (91 FR 47320–47321): "where such product's MFN tariff is greater than or equal to 10 percent [12.5 percent], the … section 301 tariff … shall be zero."
Q7.uncertainty: None as to method. Which of headings 9903.05.38/39, .48/49, .73/74, .75/76 applies to a given good depends on the annex image tables; the notice's text (91 FR 47363–47364) identifies .73–.74 as Switzerland, .75–.76 as Taiwan and .38–.39 as the EU.

The applicable rule is the DATES line: duties apply to goods entered/withdrawn on or after 12:01 a.m. ET July 24, 2026, "except that goods loaded onto a vessel at the port of loading and in transit on the final mode of transit before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 24, 2026, and entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 28, 2026, shall not be subject to such additional duty" (91 FR 47318).

Q11.answer:
Discrepancies found (each listed once):

**1. Nonexistent dairy scope proclamation.** 11062 cl. (3) (91 FR 58320) says that, besides converting products to a ban, the proclamation "does not otherwise affect the products, as further established in the Proclamation of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope of Products of Canada Subject to the Additional Duties Imposed To Offset Canadian Discrimination Against the Commerce of the United States With Respect to Dairy), that are subject to the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11047." **No such proclamation exists**: the only Sept. 8, 2026 scope modifications published are 11064 (alcoholic beverages, 91 FR 58331) and 11065 (motor vehicles, 91 FR 58339). The operative dairy text (11047 cl. (1)–(3), 91 FR 46654–46655) was never modified.

**2. "Effective August 19" recitals vs. amended operative text.** Recital 1 of each later proclamation states that section 338 duties were imposed "effective August 19, 2026": 11061 (91 FR 58311), 11062 (58319), 11063 (58325), 11064 (58331), 11065 (58339), 11076 (68861). But 11056 cl. (1) (91 FR 54790) provides that the effective date "shall be 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 22, 2026," and recital 4 of the very same later proclamations says the duties "became effective" at 12:01 a.m. on August 22, 2026.

**3. What 11056 did — "suspension" vs. change of effective date.** 11056 recitals 4–5 (91 FR 54790) describe the action as "suspending for a period of 3 days the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11046, 11047, and 11048"; its operative cl. (1) does not suspend any duty but fixes a new effective date and amends only the Annex II chapeaux. 11061 recital 2 (91 FR 58311) then says 11056 "temporarily suspended for 3 days the effective date of the additional ad valorem duties," while 11061 recital 4 says "the 3-day suspension imposed by Proclamation 11056 lapsed, and the additional ad valorem duties … became effective" — a suspended effective date cannot lapse into effect, and nothing in 11056 made the Aug. 22 date contingent on Canada's conduct.

**4. Unamended operative clauses left contrary to 11056.** 11056 cl. (1) (91 FR 54790) amended only "the chapeau of Annex II" of Proclamations 11046, 11047 and 11048. The operative clauses still read "August 19, 2026": 11046 cl. (1) and (3) (91 FR 46641); 11047 cl. (1) and (3) (46654–46655); 11048 cl. (1) and (3) (46665) — contrary to 11056's statement that the effective date "shall be" Aug. 22.

**5. Textile mechanism: "zero" vs. "reduced" rate.** The July 23, 2026 memorandum (91 FR 47719) says the Trade Representative "proposed to establish a textile mechanism that would allow a certain volume of apparel and textile imports to enter the United States at a zero section 301 tariff rate." The June 5, 2026 proposal actually stated: "a textile mechanism that would allow for a certain volume of apparel and textile imports from certain economies to enter the United States at a reduced Section 301 tariff rate" (91 FR 34272, 34274), and invited comment on "the tariff rate (if any)" (91 FR 34275).

**6. Description of the proposed 10% criterion.** The USTR notice (91 FR 47319) says the June 5 FRN "proposed applying tariffs of 10 percent for each economy that imposes a forced labor import prohibition; has taken on commitments … through an ART; or has imposed a partial regime …" without the limiting condition. The proposal itself limited the first category to economies that "impose a forced labor import prohibition but do not yet effectively enforce it (Canada, Ecuador, the European Union, Indonesia, Mexico, and Pakistan)" (memorandum recital, 91 FR 47719; see proposal at 91 FR 34274).
Q11.uncertainty: Only readable text was compared; the annex images were not reviewed, so discrepancies internal to the tariff-schedule tables (e.g., effective-date lines in the Annex II chapeaux) could not be verified. Characterization of any item as a "discrepancy" rather than a deliberate amendment is a judgment; item 4 is the clearest case of an unamended and now contrary text.

Q13.answer:
The governing text is Proclamation 11032 cl. (2) (91 FR 34087–34088), effective for entries on/after 12:01 a.m. EDT June 8, 2026 through 11:59 p.m. EST December 31, 2027, for aluminum and steel articles listed in Annex I-C: (2)(a) 25%; (2)(b) for listed jurisdictions (including Japan) a rate that brings column 1 plus 232 to 15%; (2)(c) 10% for derivatives whose aluminum/steel content is composed entirely of U.S.-smelted/melted metal; (2)(d) for USMCA-qualifying Canadian and Mexican products, "a duty of 25 percent shall apply only to the non-U.S. content of the product," where non-U.S. content = total value minus value attributable to parts produced in the United States, with a floor that "the total effective duty … shall not be less than 15 percent ad valorem." Clause (4) deems metal content U.S. only if U.S. metal is at least 85% of the product's metal by weight.

(a) Canada, USMCA claim, U.S. parts $60,000: non-U.S. content = $200,000 − $60,000 = $140,000. 25% × $140,000 = **$35,000**. Floor: 15% × $200,000 = $30,000; $35,000 > $30,000, so **$35,000**.

(b) No U.S. content: non-U.S. content = $200,000. 25% × $200,000 = **$50,000** (above the $30,000 floor).

(c) Canada, no USMCA qualification: cl. (2)(d) is unavailable and Canada is not in the cl. (2)(b) list → 25% × $200,000 = **$50,000**.

(d) Japan, MFN 2.5%: cl. (2)(b) — sum of column 1 rate and 232 rate = 15% → 232 = 12.5% × $200,000 = **$25,000**.

(e) Canada, USMCA, U.S. parts $20,000, plus $30,000 of U.S.-smelted-and-cast aluminum contained in a Canadian-made part: cl. (2)(d) counts only "parts produced in the United States," so non-U.S. content = $200,000 − $20,000 = $180,000. 25% × $180,000 = **$45,000**. The $30,000 of U.S. metal does not reduce non-U.S. content, and the 10% rate in cl. (2)(c) is unavailable because most of the metal was melted/smelted outside the United States (cl. (4) 85% test fails).

(f) Same as (e), entered Oct. 6, 2026: **$45,000**. Nothing in the documents changes the cl. (2) rate between Oct. 6 and Oct. 20, 2026; cl. (2) runs continuously from June 8, 2026 to Dec. 31, 2027.

(g) U.S. parts $140,000: non-U.S. content = $60,000; 25% × $60,000 = $15,000, which is below the floor of 15% × $200,000 = **$30,000** → duty = **$30,000**.

(h) The (a) treatment applies until **11:59 p.m. eastern standard time on December 31, 2027** (cl. (2)). Afterwards, cl. (3)(a) provides that for Annex I-C products the rates are "the rates set out in clause (3) of Proclamation 11021" — i.e., the generally applicable 25% rate (with the lower rates specified in that clause) from 12:01 a.m. EST January 1, 2028.
Q13.uncertainty: The 15% floor in cl. (2)(d) is applied to the customs value; the text says "15 percent ad valorem" without expressly defining the base, and Annex IV (an image) is said to detail the assessment. Clause (2)(c)'s 10% rate is not applied because the scenario rules out the 85% U.S.-metal test; if the machine were treated as a "derivative article" with entirely U.S. metal content the answer would differ.

Q14.answer:
1. **Partly correct.** The memorandum's operative text sets no date: §2(a)–(b) directs the Trade Representative to establish the TRQs "[a]s soon as the Trade Representative determines that it is feasible" (91 FR 47720). September 1, 2026 appears only in a recital: USTR advised that establishing the TRQs "is not feasible at this time, but that establishing these TRQs will be feasible by September 1, 2026" (91 FR 47720).

2. **Incorrect.** The notice states USTR "received over 1,600 written comments" and "over 100 witnesses provided testimony" (91 FR 47319, 47328); the memorandum repeats "over 1,600 written comments and testimony from over 100 witnesses" (91 FR 47719).

3. **Partly correct.** Seven economies took post-June-5 steps — Cambodia, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Sri Lanka and Trinidad and Tobago imposed prohibitions, and Jordan undertook ART commitments (notice 91 FR 47319; memorandum 91 FR 47720) — but only five moved from a proposed 12.5% to 10% (Honduras, India, Jordan, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago); Cambodia and Guatemala were already proposed at 10% (June 5 notice, 91 FR 34274), and Jordan's basis was an ART commitment, not an adopted ban.

4. **Incorrect.** USTR declined: "the Trade Representative has determined not to remove these products from the list of exempted products" (91 FR 47331), referring to beef, avocados, paprika, lithium hexafluorophosphate and forgings.

5. **Incorrect.** Japan and South Korea are net-of-MFN economies but have no economy-specific list: their determinations cite only "Annex I and Annex II, Part A" (91 FR 47324–47327), and note 52(j) contains no Japan or Korea list (91 FR 47363–47365).

6. **Partly correct.** USTR exempted "an additional 471 products" (91 FR 47331); but the sugar exemption covers only "certain sugar and sugar containing products," discussed as "in-quota imports of certain sugar and sugar-containing products" (91 FR 47331–47332) — not all sugar.

7. **Incorrect.** Note 52(a) (91 FR 47352) provides that products subject to the additional duties "shall also be subject to the general rates of duty imposed under subheadings in chapters 1 to 97" and to any other additional duty in the subchapter; the 12.5%/10% figure is only the section 301 rate, and the sum-of-MFN-plus-301 cap applies only to the listed net-of-MFN headings (note 52(k), 91 FR 47394; memorandum §1(a)(ii), 91 FR 47720).

8. **Correct** as a statement of the notice: products subject to the duty, except those eligible for "domestic status" under 19 CFR 146.43, "only may be admitted as 'privileged foreign status,' as defined in 19 CFR 146.41, effective as of the date that the additional duty is imposed" (91 FR 47321).

9. **Correct** (as to exemptions): "If any exemption … is held to be invalid in whole or in part, only that exemption or that part … should be treated as invalid … The applicable tariff action … would apply to imports of a product … to which the invalidated exemption … applied before its invalidation" (91 FR 47335; memorandum quoted at 47335).

10. **Correct.** "[T]he Trade Representative has determined to exempt all of the products proposed for exemption in Annex A to the June 5, 2026 FRN, except the non-pharmaceutical applications of certain chemical products," and "determined not to remove additional products from the exemption list" (91 FR 47330).
Q14.uncertainty: Statement 8's FTZ rule appears in the notice's preamble and is not restated in the readable text of U.S. note 52 (it may be carried in the image annex headings). Statement 3's count depends on how one classifies the EU's and Taiwan's shift from 10% flat to 10% net of MFN; the documents do not discuss that shift in those terms.

Q15.answer:
Additional duties on $100,000 of Canadian aluminum extrusions (7604), by authority. 232 aluminum: 10% before 12:01 a.m. Mar. 12, 2025 (Proc. 10895 cl. (2), 90 FR 9810); 25% from Mar. 12, 2025; 50% from 12:01 a.m. EDT June 4, 2025 (Proc. 10947 cl. (1), 90 FR 24200); 50% continues under Proc. 11021 cl. (2)(a) for Annex I-A articles from Apr. 6, 2026 (91 FR 18203–18204), unchanged for these goods by Proc. 11032 (Annex I-C does not cover them). Section 338: 50% from Aug. 22, 2026, but the 232 carve-out in 11048 cl. (2) removes it for 232 articles until the 11065 amendment takes effect Sept. 15, 2026; from Sept. 15 it applies in addition to 232 (11065 cl. (1), 91 FR 58340). Section 301: 10% for Canada from July 24, 2026, but note 52(f)(1) exempts derivative aluminum articles in heading 9903.82.02 and note 52(g) exempts USMCA-free Canadian goods (91 FR 47362) — so $0 in both cases. IEEPA northern-border duties (EO 14193 as amended): 25% (35% from Aug. 1, 2025) for non-USMCA goods; USMCA-free goods exempt only from Mar. 7, 2025 (EO 14231); terminated by EO 14389 (Feb. 20, 2026). 10% section 122 surcharge (Proc. 11012): Feb. 24–July 24, 2026, but 232-subject articles exempt (recital 14(k)).

Why each other additional duty is not owed:
- **IEEPA northern-border duties (EO 14193 as amended):** not in effect on Feb. 10, 2025 (imposition postponed to Mar. 4, 2025 by EO 14197); owed on Mar. 6/10/14, June 3/10 and Aug. 5, 2025 at the rates shown (25%; 35% from Aug. 1, 2025 by EO 14325); exempt for USMCA-free goods from Mar. 7, 2025 (EO 14231 §2(a)); terminated for all entries after Feb. 20, 2026 by EO 14389 (91 FR 9437).
- **Section 301:** not in force before July 24, 2026; from then, exempt because the goods are entered under 9903.82.02, a heading listed in note 52(f)(1) (91 FR 47362); in Case U also exempt under note 52(g).
- **Section 338:** not in force before Aug. 22, 2026; from Aug. 22 to Sept. 14, 2026 barred by 11048 cl. (2)'s section 232 carve-out (91 FR 46665); owed from Sept. 15, 2026.
- **10% section 122 surcharge:** never owed — Feb. 24 to July 24, 2026 only (Proc. 11012, 91 FR 9339), and exempt as a 232-subject article (recital 14(k), 91 FR 9341).

Q15.uncertainty: The 232 aluminum rate for the Feb. 10, 2025 entry (10%) is taken from Proclamation 10895's recital that the prior rate was 10% and its clause (2) raising it to 25% on Mar. 12, 2025; no separate 10% rate clause was re-read. The surcharge's 232 exemption is stated in recital 14(k) with reference to image annexes; the expiry date (July 24, 2026) is computed from "150 days … effective February 24, 2026" because no termination or extension notice appears in the Federal Register. Whether the 12% contingent rate in EO 14257 §(e) ever became operative is not established by any published document, and in any event the order imposing it was terminated by EO 14389.

Q1.uncertainty: The annexes (product lists) are images and were not readable; only the readable rule text was used. Filing-with-OFR dates appear only in the closing "Filed" lines (e.g., 11076: Filed 10-29-26). Whether any particular product is on Annex II, Annex I Part A/B or an exclusion Annex must come from the scenario, not the text.

Q2.answer:
(a) All three entries are of the same Annex II wine ($40,000 customs value, 50% rate). The controlling text is cl. (1) of Proclamation 11046 as amended by cl. (1) of Proclamation 11056: the duty applies "effective for goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 22, 2026."
- Entry 1 (Aug. 20, 2:00 p.m.): before the effective time → **$0**. ($40,000 × 50% = $20,000, but the duty does not yet apply.)
- Entry 2 (Aug. 21, 11:59 p.m.): one minute before the effective time → **$0**.
- Entry 3 (Aug. 22, 12:01 a.m.): at the effective time, and "on or after" includes that instant → 50% × $40,000 = **$20,000**.

(b) Proclamation 11056 cl. (1) (91 FR 54790) states: "The effective date of the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamations 11046, 11047, and 11048 shall be 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 22, 2026," and then amends **only** "the chapeau of Annex II of each of Proclamations 11046, 11047, and 11048" by deleting "August 19, 2026" and inserting "August 22, 2026." What was **not** amended: the operative clauses of the three base proclamations — cl. (1) and cl. (3) of 11046 (91 FR 46641), and their counterparts in 11047 (46654–46655) and 11048 (46665) — which still print "August 19, 2026." The difference is resolved by the later, specific operative direction in 11056 cl. (1) itself (the effective date "shall be" Aug. 22), reinforced by 11056 cl. (5) (inconsistent earlier provisions superseded to the extent of inconsistency, 91 FR 54791) and by the later proclamations, which state that "at 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 22, 2026, the 3-day suspension imposed by Proclamation 11056 lapsed, and the additional ad valorem duties imposed under Proclamation 11046 became effective" (11061 recital 4, 91 FR 58311; same recital 4 in 11064 at 58331, 11065 at 58339, 11076 at 68861).

(c) Proclamation 11056 cl. (4) (91 FR 54791): "To the extent that implementation of this proclamation requires a refund of duties collected, refunds shall be processed pursuant to applicable law and CBP's standard procedures for such refunds." Clause (2) also directed agencies to "as soon as practicable, suspend the collection of the additional ad valorem duties" (91 FR 54790). No document states an interest entitlement, a protest right, or a specific refund form; none addresses refunds of amounts deposited for Aug. 19–21 entries other than through cl. (4).

(d) No further presidential action was needed. 11061 recital 4 (91 FR 58311) and the identical recitals in 11064/11065/11076 state that the duties "became effective" automatically when the 3-day suspension lapsed at 12:01 a.m. on Aug. 22. As to the days before: 11056 recital 4 (54790) records Canada's expressed commitment to remove the discrimination; the later proclamations state that "[o]n August 21, 2026, Canada reneged on its commitment, ceased negotiating in good faith, and did not remove the discrimination" (11061 recital 3, 91 FR 58311; 11064 recital 3, 58331; 11065 recital 3, 58339; 11076 recital 3, 68861), and 11061 recital 5 adds Saskatchewan's Aug. 27, 2026 announced 50% levy.

(e) Recital 10 of 11046 (91 FR 46640–46641) quotes section 338: duties may "not … take effect earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation" finding the discrimination. Proclamation 11046 was signed July 20, 2026 (91 FR 46639). Arithmetic: July 20 + 30 days = **August 19, 2026**; hence recital 9 (46639) and cl. (1) fixed "12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 19, 2026" — the earliest lawful moment. (The amended date, Aug. 22, is 33 days after signing and so also satisfies the 30-day minimum.)
Q2.uncertainty: The text does not say which entry date governs for goods entered exactly at 12:01 a.m.; the "on or after" wording is read literally. The documents do not say whether a refund under 11056 cl. (4) carries interest, and they do not describe any procedure beyond "CBP's standard procedures."

Q3.answer:
The beer is dutiable under 11046 (Annex II), was not removed by 11064, and is on the Annex to 11061. The ban in 11061 cl. (1) applies to goods **imported on or after 12:01 a.m. ET Sept. 29, 2026**; cl. (2) keeps the 50% duty on goods imported before that time but not yet entered or withdrawn (91 FR 58312). Value $30,000; 50% = $15,000 per shipment.

(a)
- **A** (arrives Sept. 10; entered Sept. 14): imported before Sept. 29 and entered before Sept. 29 → may be imported; duty 50% × $30,000 = **$15,000** (11046 cl. (1) as amended).
- **B** (arrives Sept. 27; bonded warehouse; withdrawn Oct. 5): imported before Sept. 29, so not banned; cl. (2) of 11061 keeps it "subject to the 50 percent duty rate established by Proclamation 11046" → **$15,000** on the Oct. 5 withdrawal.
- **C** (arrives 11:30 p.m. Sept. 28; entry 9:00 a.m. Sept. 29): imported before Sept. 29 → not banned; it was "imported, but not yet entered for consumption … prior to September 29, 2026," so cl. (2) applies → **$15,000**.
- **D** (arrives 12:30 a.m. Sept. 29): imported on/after the effective time → **excluded from importation**; no consumption entry may be made. No section 338 duty arises because there is no lawful importation (the duty is replaced by the ban).

(b) **E** (arrives Sept. 25; admitted to an FTZ Sept. 25; entry for consumption from the zone Oct. 6): because it was admitted to the zone after the Aug. 22 effective date, 11046 cl. (4) (91 FR 46641) requires admission in "privileged foreign status" (unless domestic status applies), and on entry for consumption it is subject to the ad valorem rate for its heading. On the exclusion side, E was imported before Sept. 29, so 11061 cl. (2) applies: it "will remain subject to the 50 percent duty rate" → **50% × $30,000 = $15,000**, and no import ban.

(c) If a court invalidates the import ban as applied to this beer, 11061 cl. (9)(b) (91 FR 58313) provides that "the 50 percent ad valorem duty imposed in Proclamation 11046 shall apply to the import to which the invalidated import ban … had applied before its invalidation." So later shipments of the beer would be importable and dutiable at **50%** under Proclamation 11046.

(d) No. 11061 cl. (3) (91 FR 58312) states that, besides converting listed products from duty to ban, "this proclamation does not otherwise affect the products, as further established in the Proclamation of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope … With Respect to Alcoholic Beverages), that are subject to the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11046." Listed Canadian alcoholic products not in the Annex therefore remain subject to the 50% duty as modified by 11064.
Q3.uncertainty: The documents nowhere address the treatment of goods held in a foreign trade zone when the ban's effective date passes; the outcome in (b) rests on 11061 cl. (2)'s "imported, but not yet entered" rule plus 11046 cl. (4), and would be different if "imported" were read to mean the customs entry rather than arrival. For (d) the text is clear; for (c) the text does not say whether the 50% duty applies retroactively to goods denied entry while the ban was in force.

Q4.answer:
Section 232 duty is 25% × $100,000 = $25,000 for each product on both dates. The section 338 question turns on whether the 232 carve-out still applies.

(a) Entries Sept. 10, 2026 (before the Sept. 15 scope modifications):
- **X** (alcoholic beverages): 232 **$25,000**; section 338 **$0** (11046 cl. (2): duties "shall not apply to articles subject to duties pursuant to section 232"); total $25,000.
- **Y** (dairy): 232 **$25,000**; section 338 **$0** (11047 cl. (2)); total $25,000.
- **Z** (motor vehicles): 232 **$25,000**; section 338 **$0** (11048 cl. (2)); total $25,000.

(b) Entries Oct. 1, 2026:

Bases: P became subject when 11065 cl. (1) took effect for entries on/after 12:01 a.m. ET Sept. 15, 2026 (91 FR 58340). Q was dutiable under 11048 from Aug. 22 and was removed by 11065 Annex I, Part B, also effective Sept. 15 (same clause). R was dutiable from Aug. 22 and was removed by 11076 Annex I, Part A, effective 12:01 a.m. ET Oct. 30, 2026 (91 FR 68862) — so it is still dutiable on Oct. 29 at 4:00 p.m. S became subject only when 11076 Annex I, Part B took effect at 12:01 a.m. Oct. 30 (same clause).

(b) Proclamation 11076: **signed October 23, 2026**; **filed with the Office of the Federal Register October 29, 2026** (closing line "Filed 10-29-26; 11:15 am"); **published October 30, 2026** at 91 FR 68861. It applies from **12:01 a.m. ET October 30, 2026** to goods "entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption" (cl. (1)–(2), 91 FR 68862). The scope proclamations do **not** reach earlier entries: both 11065 and 11076 are expressly limited to entries/withdrawals on or after their effective times, and neither contains any retroactivity, refund or retroactive-relief provision (compare 11056 cl. (4), 91 FR 54791, which does address refunds).

(c) Section 338's waiting period is quoted in each scope proclamation: duties may "not … take effect earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation" (11065 recital 8, 91 FR 58340; 11076 recital 9, 91 FR 68862). P became dutiable **7 days** after signing (Sept. 8 → Sept. 15); S became dutiable **7 days** after signing (Oct. 23 → Oct. 30). Neither proclamation explains how a 7-day effective date fits the 30-day period. They characterize the action only as "modifying the scope of products" already subject to section 338 duties imposed after the July 20, 2026 finding (11065 recitals 6–7, 58340; 11076 recitals 7–8, 68862); no recital states that the 30-day clock ran from the July 20, 2026 proclamation or otherwise addresses the waiting period for newly covered products.
Q5.uncertainty: Whether a scope modification that adds products is a "new duty" subject to the 30-day waiting period is not addressed anywhere in the text; the proclamations are silent, and no amendment of section 338 is published in these documents.

Q7.answer:
(a) France (EU, 10% net of MFN). MFN duty: 3¢ × 2,000 kg = $60. Ad valorem equivalent = $60 ÷ $12,000 = **0.5%**. Section 301 = 10% − 0.5% = 9.5% → 0.095 × $12,000 = **$1,140**.

(b) MFN: 4% × $20,000 = $800, plus 25¢ × 4,000 kg = $1,000 → **$1,800**; AVE = $1,800 ÷ $20,000 = **9%**.
- **Italy (EU)**: 10% − 9% = 1% → **$200**.
- **Japan**: 12.5% − 9% = 3.5% → **$700**.
- **Brazil**: 12.5% flat → **$2,500**.

(c) MFN = $2,200 ÷ $20,000 = **11%**.
- **Taiwan**: at or above 10% → section 301 = **$0**.
- **Switzerland**: below 12.5% → 12.5% − 11% = 1.5% → **$300**.

(d) The rule is in U.S. note 52(k) to subchapter III of chapter 99, HTSUS, added by Annex I to the USTR notice at **91 FR 47394**: "for any good of a member state of the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland or Taiwan subject to a specific or compound rate of duty under column 1-General, the ad valorem equivalent rate of duty … shall be determined by dividing the amount of duty payable under column 1-General by the customs value of the good" (with a worked example of 50¢/kg on a $10/kg good = 5%). The result where the equivalent rate is at or above the cap appears in the same subdivision (91 FR 47394): "For headings 9903.05.39 and 9903.05.76, articles for which the applicable column 1 duty rate is less than 10 percent, the sum of the column 1 duty rate and the additional ad valorem rate of duty is 10 percent"; "For headings 9903.05.49, 9903.05.71 and 9903.05.74, articles for which the applicable column 1 duty rate is less than 12.5 percent, the sum … is 12.5 percent" — and the zero-at-or-above-the-cap result is stated in the memorandum §1(a)(ii) (91 FR 47720) and the notice (91 FR 47320–47321): "where such product's MFN tariff is greater than or equal to 10 percent [12.5 percent], the … section 301 tariff … shall be zero."

Q11.answer:
Discrepancies found (each listed once):

**1. Nonexistent dairy scope proclamation.** 11062 cl. (3) (91 FR 58320) says that, besides converting products to a ban, the proclamation "does not otherwise affect the products, as further established in the Proclamation of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope of Products of Canada Subject to the Additional Duties Imposed To Offset Canadian Discrimination Against the Commerce of the United States With Respect to Dairy), that are subject to the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11047." **No such proclamation exists**: the only Sept. 8, 2026 scope modifications published are 11064 (alcoholic beverages, 91 FR 58331) and 11065 (motor vehicles, 91 FR 58339). The operative dairy text (11047 cl. (1)–(3), 91 FR 46654–46655) was never modified.

**2. "Effective August 19" recitals vs. amended operative text.** Recital 1 of each later proclamation states that section 338 duties were imposed "effective August 19, 2026": 11061 (91 FR 58311), 11062 (58319), 11063 (58325), 11064 (58331), 11065 (58339), 11076 (68861). But 11056 cl. (1) (91 FR 54790) provides that the effective date "shall be 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 22, 2026," and recital 4 of the very same later proclamations says the duties "became effective" at 12:01 a.m. on August 22, 2026.

**3. What 11056 did — "suspension" vs. change of effective date.** 11056 recitals 4–5 (91 FR 54790) describe the action as "suspending for a period of 3 days the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11046, 11047, and 11048"; its operative cl. (1) does not suspend any duty but fixes a new effective date and amends only the Annex II chapeaux. 11061 recital 2 (91 FR 58311) then says 11056 "temporarily suspended for 3 days the effective date of the additional ad valorem duties," while 11061 recital 4 says "the 3-day suspension imposed by Proclamation 11056 lapsed, and the additional ad valorem duties … became effective" — a suspended effective date cannot lapse into effect, and nothing in 11056 made the Aug. 22 date contingent on Canada's conduct.

**4. Unamended operative clauses left contrary to 11056.** 11056 cl. (1) (91 FR 54790) amended only "the chapeau of Annex II" of Proclamations 11046, 11047 and 11048. The operative clauses still read "August 19, 2026": 11046 cl. (1) and (3) (91 FR 46641); 11047 cl. (1) and (3) (46654–46655); 11048 cl. (1) and (3) (46665) — contrary to 11056's statement that the effective date "shall be" Aug. 22.

**5. Textile mechanism: "zero" vs. "reduced" rate.** The July 23, 2026 memorandum (91 FR 47719) says the Trade Representative "proposed to establish a textile mechanism that would allow a certain volume of apparel and textile imports to enter the United States at a zero section 301 tariff rate." The June 5, 2026 proposal actually stated: "a textile mechanism that would allow for a certain volume of apparel and textile imports from certain economies to enter the United States at a reduced Section 301 tariff rate" (91 FR 34272, 34274), and invited comment on "the tariff rate (if any)" (91 FR 34275).

**6. Description of the proposed 10% criterion.** The USTR notice (91 FR 47319) says the June 5 FRN "proposed applying tariffs of 10 percent for each economy that imposes a forced labor import prohibition; has taken on commitments … through an ART; or has imposed a partial regime …" without the limiting condition. The proposal itself limited the first category to economies that "impose a forced labor import prohibition but do not yet effectively enforce it (Canada, Ecuador, the European Union, Indonesia, Mexico, and Pakistan)" (memorandum recital, 91 FR 47719; see proposal at 91 FR 34274).
Q11.uncertainty: Only readable text was compared; the annex images were not reviewed, so discrepancies internal to the tariff-schedule tables (e.g., effective-date lines in the Annex II chapeaux) could not be verified. Characterization of any item as a "discrepancy" rather than a deliberate amendment is a judgment; item 4 is the clearest case of an unamended and now contrary text.

The governing text is Proclamation 11032 cl. (2) (91 FR 34087–34088), effective for entries on/after 12:01 a.m. EDT June 8, 2026 through 11:59 p.m. EST December 31, 2027, for aluminum and steel articles listed in Annex I-C: (2)(a) 25%; (2)(b) for listed jurisdictions (including Japan) a rate that brings column 1 plus 232 to 15%; (2)(c) 10% for derivatives whose aluminum/steel content is composed entirely of U.S.-smelted/melted metal; (2)(d) for USMCA-qualifying Canadian and Mexican products, "a duty of 25 percent shall apply only to the non-U.S. content of the product," where non-U.S. content = total value minus value attributable to parts produced in the United States, with a floor that "the total effective duty … shall not be less than 15 percent ad valorem." Clause (4) deems metal content U.S. only if U.S. metal is at least 85% of the product's metal by weight.

(a) Canada, USMCA claim, U.S. parts $60,000: non-U.S. content = $200,000 − $60,000 = $140,000. 25% × $140,000 = **$35,000**. Floor: 15% × $200,000 = $30,000; $35,000 > $30,000, so **$35,000**.

(b) No U.S. content: non-U.S. content = $200,000. 25% × $200,000 = **$50,000** (above the $30,000 floor).

(c) Canada, no USMCA qualification: cl. (2)(d) is unavailable and Canada is not in the cl. (2)(b) list → 25% × $200,000 = **$50,000**.

(d) Japan, MFN 2.5%: cl. (2)(b) — sum of column 1 rate and 232 rate = 15% → 232 = 12.5% × $200,000 = **$25,000**.

(e) Canada, USMCA, U.S. parts $20,000, plus $30,000 of U.S.-smelted-and-cast aluminum contained in a Canadian-made part: cl. (2)(d) counts only "parts produced in the United States," so non-U.S. content = $200,000 − $20,000 = $180,000. 25% × $180,000 = **$45,000**. The $30,000 of U.S. metal does not reduce non-U.S. content, and the 10% rate in cl. (2)(c) is unavailable because most of the metal was melted/smelted outside the United States (cl. (4) 85% test fails).

(f) Same as (e), entered Oct. 6, 2026: **$45,000**. Nothing in the documents changes the cl. (2) rate between Oct. 6 and Oct. 20, 2026; cl. (2) runs continuously from June 8, 2026 to Dec. 31, 2027.

(g) U.S. parts $140,000: non-U.S. content = $60,000; 25% × $60,000 = $15,000, which is below the floor of 15% × $200,000 = **$30,000** → duty = **$30,000**.

(h) The (a) treatment applies until **11:59 p.m. eastern standard time on December 31, 2027** (cl. (2)). Afterwards, cl. (3)(a) provides that for Annex I-C products the rates are "the rates set out in clause (3) of Proclamation 11021" — i.e., the generally applicable 25% rate (with the lower rates specified in that clause) from 12:01 a.m. EST January 1, 2028.
Q13.uncertainty: The 15% floor in cl. (2)(d) is applied to the customs value; the text says "15 percent ad valorem" without expressly defining the base, and Annex IV (an image) is said to detail the assessment. Clause (2)(c)'s 10% rate is not applied because the scenario rules out the 85% U.S.-metal test; if the machine were treated as a "derivative article" with entirely U.S. metal content the answer would differ.

Q14.answer:
1. **Partly correct.** The memorandum's operative text sets no date: §2(a)–(b) directs the Trade Representative to establish the TRQs "[a]s soon as the Trade Representative determines that it is feasible" (91 FR 47720). September 1, 2026 appears only in a recital: USTR advised that establishing the TRQs "is not feasible at this time, but that establishing these TRQs will be feasible by September 1, 2026" (91 FR 47720).

2. **Incorrect.** The notice states USTR "received over 1,600 written comments" and "over 100 witnesses provided testimony" (91 FR 47319, 47328); the memorandum repeats "over 1,600 written comments and testimony from over 100 witnesses" (91 FR 47719).

3. **Partly correct.** Seven economies took post-June-5 steps — Cambodia, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Sri Lanka and Trinidad and Tobago imposed prohibitions, and Jordan undertook ART commitments (notice 91 FR 47319; memorandum 91 FR 47720) — but only five moved from a proposed 12.5% to 10% (Honduras, India, Jordan, Sri Lanka, Trinidad and Tobago); Cambodia and Guatemala were already proposed at 10% (June 5 notice, 91 FR 34274), and Jordan's basis was an ART commitment, not an adopted ban.

4. **Incorrect.** USTR declined: "the Trade Representative has determined not to remove these products from the list of exempted products" (91 FR 47331), referring to beef, avocados, paprika, lithium hexafluorophosphate and forgings.

5. **Incorrect.** Japan and South Korea are net-of-MFN economies but have no economy-specific list: their determinations cite only "Annex I and Annex II, Part A" (91 FR 47324–47327), and note 52(j) contains no Japan or Korea list (91 FR 47363–47365).

6. **Partly correct.** USTR exempted "an additional 471 products" (91 FR 47331); but the sugar exemption covers only "certain sugar and sugar containing products," discussed as "in-quota imports of certain sugar and sugar-containing products" (91 FR 47331–47332) — not all sugar.

7. **Incorrect.** Note 52(a) (91 FR 47352) provides that products subject to the additional duties "shall also be subject to the general rates of duty imposed under subheadings in chapters 1 to 97" and to any other additional duty in the subchapter; the 12.5%/10% figure is only the section 301 rate, and the sum-of-MFN-plus-301 cap applies only to the listed net-of-MFN headings (note 52(k), 91 FR 47394; memorandum §1(a)(ii), 91 FR 47720).

8. **Correct** as a statement of the notice: products subject to the duty, except those eligible for "domestic status" under 19 CFR 146.43, "only may be admitted as 'privileged foreign status,' as defined in 19 CFR 146.41, effective as of the date that the additional duty is imposed" (91 FR 47321).

9. **Correct** (as to exemptions): "If any exemption … is held to be invalid in whole or in part, only that exemption or that part … should be treated as invalid … The applicable tariff action … would apply to imports of a product … to which the invalidated exemption … applied before its invalidation" (91 FR 47335; memorandum quoted at 47335).

10. **Correct.** "[T]he Trade Representative has determined to exempt all of the products proposed for exemption in Annex A to the June 5, 2026 FRN, except the non-pharmaceutical applications of certain chemical products," and "determined not to remove additional products from the exemption list" (91 FR 47330).
Q14.uncertainty: Statement 8's FTZ rule appears in the notice's preamble and is not restated in the readable text of U.S. note 52 (it may be carried in the image annex headings). Statement 3's count depends on how one classifies the EU's and Taiwan's shift from 10% flat to 10% net of MFN; the documents do not discuss that shift in those terms.

Why each other additional duty is not owed:
- **IEEPA northern-border duties (EO 14193 as amended):** not in effect on Feb. 10, 2025 (imposition postponed to Mar. 4, 2025 by EO 14197); owed on Mar. 6/10/14, June 3/10 and Aug. 5, 2025 at the rates shown (25%; 35% from Aug. 1, 2025 by EO 14325); exempt for USMCA-free goods from Mar. 7, 2025 (EO 14231 §2(a)); terminated for all entries after Feb. 20, 2026 by EO 14389 (91 FR 9437).

Q15.uncertainty: The 232 aluminum rate for the Feb. 10, 2025 entry (10%) is taken from Proclamation 10895's recital that the prior rate was 10% and its clause (2) raising it to 25% on Mar. 12, 2025; no separate 10% rate clause was re-read. The surcharge's 232 exemption is stated in recital 14(k) with reference to image annexes; the expiry date (July 24, 2026) is computed from "150 days … effective February 24, 2026" because no termination or extension notice appears in the Federal Register. Whether the 12% contingent rate in EO 14257 §(e) ever became operative is not established by any published document, and in any event the order imposing it was terminated by EO 14389.
